risks.title: PACE_SOURCE_IN ESTIMATED path is registry-valid but never emitted
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (deferral originally made and documented in Phase 4D.2 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: The runtime condition registry defines PACE_SOURCE_IN.ESTIMATED as a valid value, but Backend Integration Phase 4D.2's PaceSourceResolver deliberately never emits it: no approved estimation methodology was found anywhere in the repository for deriving a pace source from runningBackground / recentWeeklyVolumeKm / recentLongestRunKm / recentRunsPerWeek alone. As a result, a user who supplies training-volume evidence but no recent race result and no target finish time currently resolves to NONE, not ESTIMATED. This is acceptable while the resolver remains unwired from live generation, but it is activation-relevant: before PACE_SOURCE_IN output is ever consumed by real plan generation, product must decide how this user population should be classified.
affectedAreas: RUNTIME_CONDITION_VALUES_V1 v2 (PACE_SOURCE_IN.ESTIMATED)
PaceSourceResolver
future runtime generation / pace-source-dependent logic
requiredResolution: Approve and document a V1 estimation methodology for ESTIMATED (e.g. from training-volume evidence), and implement it in PaceSourceResolver; or
Explicitly decide V1 will not use ESTIMATED at all and update registry/docs accordingly (e.g. mark it reserved-for-future-version); or
Keep ESTIMATED reserved but explicitly confirm product/UX accepts NONE as the outcome for training-volume-only users.
Do not implement an unapproved estimation method to close this risk.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4D.5.1 (cross-risk finding, discovered during Phase 4D.5 orchestration testing): if the ESTIMATED path described above is later implemented, OR PaceSourceResolver's output priority (currently RECENT_RACE > TARGET_TIME > NONE) changes for any other reason, re-verify GoalFeasibilityResolver behavior for the combination PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE with targetFinishTimeSeconds present. Reason: as of Phase 4D.5, GoalFeasibilityResolver's own PACE_SOURCE_NONE_TARGET_TIME_REQUESTED branch is unreachable through real RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAll orchestration, because PaceSourceResolver already emits TARGET_TIME (not NONE) whenever targetFinishTimeSeconds exists -- GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN never sees PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE while a target time is also present under the current pipeline. This is a behavioral dependency between the two resolvers' logic, not a type-system guarantee -- nothing prevents a future change to PaceSourceResolver's priority order (e.g. if ESTIMATED is introduced ahead of TARGET_TIME, or the priority order is otherwise revised) from making this branch reachable again with different semantics than originally intended. See PHASE4D_5_RUNTIME_CONDITION_RESOLVER_ORCHESTRATION_SERVICE.md ('a new finding') and PHASE4D_5_1_PACESOURCE_GOALFEASIBILITY_CROSS_RISK_NOTE.md for full detail. risks.title: AsOfDate preview/confirm lifecycle semantics not wired
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (field originally added in Phase 4D.2 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: PaceSourceResolver computes recent-race-evidence age (and the associated recency-confidence metadata) relative to RuntimeResolverContext.AsOfDate, an explicit evaluation-date field added in Phase 4D.2 specifically so the resolver never reads the wall clock directly. However, the live preview/confirm request lifecycle does not yet supply or persist an AsOfDate anywhere -- no code populates this field outside of tests. Before any future phase wires PaceSourceResolver into live generation, product/engineering must decide: does AsOfDate get fixed at preview-generation time and then reused unchanged at confirm (for preview/confirm consistency), or does it get recomputed fresh at confirm time (allowing recency to reflect any delay between preview and confirm)? No repository evidence resolves this question either way.
affectedAreas: RuntimeResolverContext.AsOfDate
PaceSourceResolver recency metadata
future preview/confirm lifecycle wiring
requiredResolution: Decide whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate or recomputes it independently.
Wire whichever behavior is chosen into the live preview/confirm flow when PaceSourceResolver is eventually connected to generation.
Do not silently default to wall-clock time at confirm without an explicit product decision.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN recency metadata (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4E.1.1 (governance clarification pass): Phase 4E.1 computed AsOfDate exactly once per preview (DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.UtcNow), never re-read per resolver) and threaded it unchanged through the pilot resolver pipeline and into the frozen CatalogPreviewSnapshot.AsOfDate field -- see PHASE4E_1_CATALOG_PREVIEW_ROUTING_AND_IMMUTABLE_RESOLUTION_SNAPSHOT.md section 7. This satisfies the preview-side half of PaceSourceResolver's own AsOfDate contract, but does NOT touch this TD's actual closure criteria, all three of which are about CONFIRM: whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate unchanged or recomputes it independently, and wiring that decision in. Phase 4E.1 does not wire catalog generation into confirm at all (by design), so none of the three requiredResolution items are satisfied yet. Intended closure path: Phase 4E.2, which must read the frozen AsOfDate from the stored CatalogPreviewSnapshot at confirm time and make (and wire) an explicit reuse-vs-recompute decision -- never silently default to wall-clock time at confirm. This TD may legitimately remain OPEN even after Phase 4E.2 ships if that phase implements snapshot-reuse mechanically without an explicit, recorded product decision on which policy (reuse vs. recompute) is correct. Backend Integration Phase 4E.2 acceptance-finalization pass addendum (appended, not replacing the above; status NOT changed to closed -- reconciled per PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 17 and PHASE4E_2_FINAL_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md): CatalogPlanConfirmationService.BuildPlan now explicitly reads StartedAt from snapshot.AsOfDate and never recomputes it from DateTime.UtcNow (ConfirmedAtUtc is kept strictly separate, technical-only). RESOLVED by this: (a) preview freezes AsOfDate exactly once; (b) confirm code, where wired, does not recompute AsOfDate; (c) confirm does not rerun resolver orchestration to derive AsOfDate or anything else; (d) an immutable preview/confirm snapshot-consistency boundary now exists in code. UNRESOLVED, and NOT covered by this TD's own tracked closure criteria: persistable stage-to-week schedule generation (GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload is still always null -- BuildPlan's AsOfDate-reuse code is not reachable in production because the step-11 persistability guard rejects every real snapshot first, so the reuse decision has never been exercised against real traffic); calendar-day alignment (does not exist); production concurrent-confirmation safety (no DB-level preview-to-plan uniqueness invariant exists -- tracked as a Blocking Defect in PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 15, not part of this TD's own scope); and public catalog activation (still blocked by the PUBLISHED-only eligibility gate, independently of this TD). This TD is NOT closed: its own three requiredResolution items are substantively addressed by (a)-(d) above, but the repository's established convention (see TD-CORE-READINESS-001's own precedent) is not to mechanically close a risk whose implementation has not yet been exercised against real, live traffic -- the AsOfDate-reuse code path in BuildPlan has never actually run against a real confirm request. Re-review for closure once a future phase makes GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload reachable and this code path is genuinely exercised.

risks.title: Foundation Compression Readiness Gate Is Undefined
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3A ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â Eight-Week Race-Core Allocation Audit (governance follow-up)
risks.source: PHASE4G_3A_EIGHT_WEEK_CORE_ALLOCATION_AUDIT.md section 5a (Clarification -- N=8 mootness does not resolve the general C-03 question); backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Resolvers/CoreEntryReadinessResolver.cs; backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/Materialization/CatalogPhaseAllocation.cs; plan-catalog/catalog/templates/ten-k-master.v6.json
risks.statement: For the current exact-8-week TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE core (the only 8-week allocation the catalog's own minimums permit: F2/B3/RS2/T1), Foundation does not compress to 1 week -- the active catalog minimum for FOUNDATION is 2, so this question is not applicable to today's pilot. This does NOT resolve the general product/runtime rule for future horizons or candidates where Foundation=1 may become structurally possible (e.g. a shorter horizon, a revised candidate, or a future catalog minimum change): no confirmed repository artifact currently defines which CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN outcomes (READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY) would permit Foundation=1 if and when it becomes structurally reachable. Future horizon-aware compression work must not enable Foundation=1 without an explicit readiness-gating decision. The runtime already resolves CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN for every catalog-routed request today (CoreEntryReadinessResolver is registered in production DI and invoked by RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAllResults) and its result is already in scope at the phase-allocation call site -- so the open issue is decision/contract ownership (which readiness outcomes permit Foundation=1, and which layer decides), not absence of the signal itself.
affectedAreas: Future horizon-aware CatalogPhaseAllocationResolver (not yet implemented)
CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN consumption contract
FOUNDATION phase compression policy
Any future sub-12-week race-core implementation phase (e.g. Phase 4G.3B and beyond)
requiredResolution: Before any future allocation permits Foundation=1, explicitly define whether CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN=READY permits Foundation=1.
Explicitly define whether CAUTION permits Foundation=1, forbids it, or requires a different (non-Foundation=1) allocation instead.
Explicitly define whether NOT_READY always forbids Foundation=1.
Identify which layer owns this eligibility decision (e.g. the phase-allocation resolver itself, an upstream routing/service-layer guard, or a dedicated policy).
Define how the phase allocator consumes CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN's already-computed result without re-running or duplicating resolver evaluation.
Define the typed, fail-closed result that applies when a target horizon structurally requires Foundation=1 but the runner's CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN outcome is not eligible.

Do not enable Foundation=1 for any allocation without this decision being explicitly recorded first -- do not silently infer it from the N=8 finding, which does not apply (N8_STATUS: NOT_APPLICABLE_DUE_TO_CATALOG_MINIMUM_2).
risks.closureNote: Closed via reachability proof (Phase 4G.3B.9), not via a coaching/scientific readiness threshold. Within the current 10K N=8-14 executable scope, no allocation path ever requires Foundation below its catalog minimum, and CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN is confirmed to have zero influence on phase allocation in any current production or dark code path. The original question ('at what readiness level may Foundation compress below minimum') remains genuinely unanswered scientifically -- it is closed here only because it is currently unreachable, not because it has been resolved. This closure is explicitly scoped and must be reopened if any of the following occur: (1) the minimum supported horizon is lowered below 8 weeks for this or any candidate, (2) phase minimums become soft/overridable constraints in the allocator, or (3) CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN begins influencing phase allocation in any future phase. A brief literature check (this session) found general supporting principle -- base/foundation phases should not be compressed without limit and readiness affects safe compression -- but no directly transferable numeric threshold for this catalog's scale; this is noted for context, not used as the closure basis. Evidence (re-verified this pass, not assumed unchanged): (1) ReadinessEligibilityVerifierTests.Verify_RealFeasibleRange_OutcomeIsPass_FoundationNeverBelowCatalogMinimum, re-run this pass, exhaustively covers targetWeeks 8-14 against the real allocator/candidate and confirms Outcome=Pass with zero RequiresBelowMinimum violations at every target; a companion test pins Foundation's exact AllocatedWeeks per target (8:2, 9:2, 10:2, 11:2, 12:3, 13:4, 14:4 -- never 1). (2) A repository-wide grep for CoreEntryReadiness/CORE_ENTRY_READINESS references across all four backend production projects found 16 files; every one is either the resolver pipeline itself (TimeAdequacy/PaceSource/GoalFeasibility dependency chain, unrelated to phase week-count allocation), a documented non-dependency (CatalogPlanConfirmationService's own doc comment explicitly lists CoreEntryReadiness among resolvers it must NEVER call), a decision-trace label array (CatalogPreviewGenerator.BuildDecisionTrace, display-only), an explicit NotSupported classification (PlanCatalogDomainMapper), or DI registration (Program.cs). CatalogPhaseAllocationResolver.Resolve (both overloads, the sole phase-week-count allocator) takes only (candidate) or (candidate, targetWeekCount) -- no readiness parameter exists in its signature, and a full read of CatalogPhaseAllocation.cs found zero readiness reference outside its own doc comments explicitly disclaiming one ('no safety, readiness, or eligibility judgment'). ProgressionStageAllocator.cs's own CoreEntryReadinessResolver.ConditionTypeValue reference is a separate, downstream allocator (workout-stage eligibility within already-fixed weeks), confirmed unrelated to phase week-count allocation, which is fixed before that allocator ever runs. (3) PhaseConstraintVerifier.Verify (re-run this pass) reports Fail, unconditionally, for any AllocatedWeeks < MinimumWeeks, with no override path ("no I/O, no candidate/catalog/readiness dependency" per its own doc comment); CatalogPhaseAllocationResolver.Resolve itself structurally cannot produce a below-minimum allocation -- the compression distribution loop's own canAdjust predicate (`allocated[p.PhaseKey] > p.MinimumWeeks`) makes it unconditionally impossible, and any targetWeekCount below the sum of all minimums is rejected as IsMathematicallyFeasible=false before any per-phase distribution runs at all. Real current phase minimums re-verified directly against ten-k-master.v6.json (correcting an unverified assumption in this pass's own task prompt, which guessed BUILD=2): FOUNDATION=2, BUILD=3, RACE_SPECIFIC=2, TAPER=1.

risks.title: NotEvaluated Resolver Results Can Route to Fallback Stages Without Confirmed Product Approval -- Scope Corrected by Real E2E Characterization (Phase 4G.3B.6.1)
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3B StageReachabilityVerifier work, validation and follow-up pass (2026-07-23); scope corrected by Phase 4G.3B.6 (2026-07-24) and Phase 4G.3B.6.1 (2026-07-24)
risks.statement:
ProgressionStageAllocator.IsStageEligible computes `satisfied = result.Status == RuntimeConditionResolutionStatus.Evaluated && result.OutputValue is not null && condition.AllowedValues.Contains(result.OutputValue)`, and returns false whenever this is not true. This means a runtime condition resolver returning NotEvaluated (the resolver could not decide) and a resolver returning Evaluated with an output value outside the stage's AllowedValues (the resolver decided the condition is not met) are treated identically: both make `satisfied=false`, and ResolveEligibility then walks the stage's FallbackStageKey exactly the same way for either case. This mechanism itself still exists, unchanged, in ProgressionStageAllocator. No runtime code distinguishes 'the resolver couldn't decide' from 'the resolver decided the condition isn't met' when routing a conditional progression stage to its fallback. This was discovered during Phase 4G.3B's StageReachabilityVerifier work, which deliberately delegates all stage-selection logic to the real ProgressionStageAllocator (proving the verifier introduces no second scheduling algorithm) and in doing so surfaced this pre-existing behavior. This is structurally the same category of gap as AUD-008 / TD-ALLOCATION-PRIORITY-001: an existing runtime behavior with no traceable product/coaching approval, discovered by a verification pass rather than authored as a deliberate decision.

SCOPE CORRECTION AND RUNTIME CHARACTERIZATION (Phase 4G.3B.6 / 4G.3B.6.1): Phase 4G.3B.6 (a read-only source audit) established that GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN can resolve to NotEvaluated for a real, currently reachable 12-week pilot input -- TargetFinishTimeSource=UserDefined, TargetFinishTimeSeconds>0, and no complete RecentRace -- correctly identifying the resolver outcome and reason PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_NO_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE. That audit correctly established resolver-level reachability but inferred, from the allocator's own logic in isolation, that this NotEvaluated result would proceed to ProgressionStageAllocator's FallbackStageKey and silently select CURRENT_FITNESS_SPECIFIC_REHEARSAL for the live 12-week pilot. Phase 4G.3B.6.1 corrected that downstream inference using a real HTTP end-to-end test through the actual TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE catalog pipeline (POST /api/v1/plans/generate-preview/race, real Api host + real Postgres DB): CatalogPreviewGenerator.ApplyNotEvaluatedGovernancePolicy classifies this reason as Unsupported (per NotEvaluatedReasonClassifier) and throws RuntimeConditionUnsupportedException BEFORE stage scheduling begins. The observed public result is HTTP 422 RUNTIME_CONDITION_UNSUPPORTED, with no stage allocation, fallback stage, workout binding, dated schedule, or PlanPreview/TrainingPlan/Week/Day persistence of any kind. Therefore, silent runtime fallback to CURRENT_FITNESS_SPECIFIC_REHEARSAL is NOT currently reachable for this production trigger -- Phase 4G.3B.6's downstream-path prediction is disproved by direct observation, while its resolver-reachability finding stands confirmed. The comparable ProductAverage control (identical request, TargetFinishTimeSource=ProductAverage) remains unaffected: GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN resolves Evaluated/CHALLENGING/PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_PRODUCT_AVERAGE_ACCEPTED, HTTP 200, 12 weeks/48 sessions, fallback_used=false.

The risk remains OPEN with a narrowed and corrected scope. A real subset of currently-enabled 12-week TEN_K/Intermediate/4-day pilot users -- those entering a custom (UserDefined) target finish time without complete recent-race evidence -- are hard-blocked from plan generation entirely and receive a generic RUNTIME_CONDITION_UNSUPPORTED/422 error with no actionable product guidance distinguishing this case from any other 422. This is not merely a future 8-14-week activation concern; it is reachable today against the live pilot. It is also not the silent, undisclosed plan-quality downgrade the original statement described -- the real failure mode is a hard, explicit generation failure, not a silently substituted workout.

Separately, the offline GoalPaceReachabilityVerifier continues to unconditionally construct and evaluate a synthetic universal NotEvaluated check on every call (regardless of any specific request's actual resolved value), which is why RaceCoreSupportRegistry still reports DecisionRequired for every real 8-14-week target including the live 12-week pilot (see RaceCoreSupportRegistry's own real registry table, Phase 4G.3B.5). That verifier finding remains a valid description of the offline verifier's own conservative, universal proof obligation -- it does not claim (and this correction does not claim on its behalf) that the allocator fallback is actually reached at runtime for any specific request.

SEMANTICS CLARIFICATION (Phase 4G.3B.6.4 / 4G.3B.6.5): Runtime safety for this risk's originally identified trigger (PACE_SOURCE_TARGET_TIME_NO_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE) is confirmed -- the request fails closed with HTTP 422 before stage scheduling (Phase 4G.3B.6.1). The offline GoalPaceReachabilityVerifier's DecisionRequired classification (propagating to RaceCoreSupportRegistry for all 7 target week counts, including the live 12-week pilot) reflects an unproven universal theoretical catalog-contract completeness claim, not an observed runtime safety gap. This distinction is now documented in PHASE4G_3B_6_4_GOALPACE_VERIFIER_RUNTIME_REACHABILITY_SEMANTICS_AUDIT.md and reflected in the verifier/orchestrator/registry documentation (GoalPaceReachabilityVerifier.cs's own doc comment, PHASE4G_3B_4B_SAFETY_VERIFICATION_ORCHESTRATOR.md section 8b, and PHASE4G_3B_5_SUPPORT_REGISTRY.md section 6). Additionally: the currently-shipped Flutter client does not yet call the real generatePreview() endpoint (a mock shortcut is active), so no real user is exposed to either the ProductAverage or UserDefined path today -- this is recorded as current-impact context, not as resolution. Option C (splitting universal-completeness from runtime-reachable-safety as two distinct verifier outputs) remains explicitly deferred until a real consumer of that distinction exists -- see PHASE4G_3B_5_SUPPORT_REGISTRY.md's 'Future Option C trigger conditions' section for the exact conditions.

This TD remains OPEN. Open decisions 1-3 from the Phase 4G.3B.6.2 correction remain unresolved and unchanged by this addendum.

PHASE 4G.5G GENERALIZATION CONFIRMATION (dynamic core pace prescription, dark/unwired): Phase 4G.5G's new dark DynamicCoreSessionPrescriptionOrchestrator re-exercised this TD's downstream fallback mechanism across 7 target week counts (8-14) and 5 pace-evidence categories including a NotEvaluated PACE_SOURCE_IN/GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN combination and an Evaluated/UNSUPPORTED GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN combination (35 combinations total, real ProgressionStageAllocator/CatalogSessionPrescriptionPlanner, unmodified). Confirmed in every case: GOAL_PACE_TEN_K (the ExactPace-eligible workout) never appears in the bound/prescribed plan when goal feasibility is NotEvaluated or Unsupported -- the existing, unmodified ProgressionStageAllocator eligibility/fallback mechanism already routes these to CURRENT_FITNESS_SPECIFIC_REHEARSAL/THRESHOLD_TEMPO before the prescription layer is ever reached, so CatalogSessionPrescriptionPlanner.PaceFor's own GOAL_PACE_TEN_K fail-closed guard (CatalogGoalPacePrescriptionUnsupportedException) was never exercised because the structurally-unsafe combination it guards against does not arise. This is confirming evidence that the fail-closed philosophy (Phase 4G.3B.6.1: reject/reroute before generating, never silently substitute a numeric pace) generalizes correctly to 8-14 weeks -- it does not resolve this TD's own open product/UX decisions (items 1-3 above), which remain unchanged and unresolved. This dark orchestrator is not wired into CatalogPreviewGenerator or any live path, so it does not itself change the confirmed HTTP 422 runtime behavior for the live 12-week pilot. See PHASE4G_5G_DYNAMIC_CORE_PACE_PRESCRIPTION.md.

If so, what actionable guidance should the user receive (e.g. suggesting 'go with average' or completing a recent-race entry) instead of a generic unsupported-condition error?

Offline-verifier semantics decision: should GoalPaceReachabilityVerifier's universal synthetic NotEvaluated check continue to treat every possible NotEvaluated outcome as part of the fallback-reachability proof obligation, or should runtime-rejected NotEvaluated reason categories (Unsupported/RequiredInputNotProvided/DependencyUnresolved per NotEvaluatedReasonClassifier, which the real governance gate intercepts before scheduling) be represented separately from genuinely stage-reachable fallback cases?

Independently of the above: a product decision is still required on whether any NotEvaluated reason that DOES reach ProgressionStageAllocator uncontested should continue to silently fall back to the alternate stage (current behavior for such reasons), or should instead block/flag the affected week for a different treatment.

Do not fix or change ProgressionStageAllocator's NotEvaluated-to-fallback behavior, CatalogPreviewGenerator's governance policy, or NotEvaluatedReasonClassifier's categorization without an explicit decision being recorded first.
This risk must remain OPEN, with this corrected scope explicitly factored into any future safety-verification or support-registry work, until the above decisions are made.

risks.title: HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio and AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm Are Documented Policy Fields Never Enforced by the Real Weekly-Volume Curve
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3B VolumeProgressionVerifier implementation pass, governance follow-up (2026-07-23)
risks.statement: CatalogVolumeAndLongRunPlanner.BuildWeeklyPlan generates every non-taper week via linear interpolation from the starting volume to a transition-count-scaled reachable peak (ResolvePeak). VolumeSafetyPolicy.HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio and AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm exist as typed policy fields and are threaded into ReachablePeakDecision, but only as decision-trace provenance metadata -- neither value is ever read back to clamp or reject an actual week-to-week transition anywhere in the real curve-generation code path. VolumeProgressionVerifier independently confirmed, for the real TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE candidate across all 7 feasible target week counts (8 through 14), that every generated non-taper transition currently stays within both bounds anyway -- but this is a property of this candidate's specific starting-volume/peak interpolation shape, not a guarantee actively enforced by the planner for any future candidate, catalog revision, or target week count. Practical effect: if a future candidate/catalog combination produces a starting volume and peak whose linear interpolation would exceed HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio or AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm, nothing in the current code path would catch or prevent it -- the two policy fields would remain silently decorative. This is architecturally different from TD-FOUNDATION-COMPRESSION-001, TD-ALLOCATION-PRIORITY-001, and TD-NOTEVALUATED-FALLBACK-001, which document undecided product questions about behavior that does execute; this finding documents a safety mechanism that exists in code as a typed policy contract but is not wired to enforce anything today -- closer to a silent gap than an open decision.

VolumeProgressionVerifier (Phase 4G.3B.3, mechanical-only, not yet publicly wired)
Any future candidate, catalog revision, or target week count whose starting-volume/peak shape has not already been verified

This must be resolved, or explicitly accepted as informational-only with a documented rationale, before this planner is trusted for any candidate, catalog revision, or target week count beyond what has already been verified today (the current 8-14-week TEN_K_MASTER v6 range).
Do not silently start enforcing these fields, or silently continue treating them as decorative, without this decision being explicitly recorded first.

risks.closureNote: Resolution (Phase 4G.3B.7/4G.3B.7.1): Decision audit (Phase 4G.3B.7) proved algebraically that for TEN_K_MASTER v6's current constants, the per-transition volume-increase ratio required to reach the catalog peak within the fixed non-taper transition count is independent of starting volume and target week count, and stays structurally below both HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio and AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm by construction -- not by coincidence of the specific values tested. Enforcing these caps as active per-transition clamps was evaluated (Option A) but found to require redesigning the reachable-peak model with zero benefit to current behavior, since the caps are structurally unreachable today. Resolution: HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio and AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm are now explicitly documented as informational/provenance-only fields (Option B), not active runtime safety gates. This closure is scoped to TEN_K_MASTER v6's current constants -- see Phase 4G.3B.7/4G.3B.7.1 documentation for the exact conditions (a future candidate/catalog revision with different starting-volume/peak-volume/core-cycle constants) that would require re-running this analysis before treating a new candidate's curves as safe under the same assumption.
risks.closureCriteriaSatisfied: First requiredResolution option's second alternative fully satisfied: HardMaxWeeklyIncreaseRatio and AbsoluteWeeklyIncrementCapKm are now explicitly reclassified in VolumeSafetyPolicy's own documentation (and PHASE4G_3B_0_VOLUME_SAFETY_POLICY_GOVERNANCE_NOTE.md, and VolumeProgressionVerifier.cs) as informational/provenance-only fields that do not function as runtime safety gates, with a documented, algebraically-proven rationale (Phase 4G.3B.7) rather than an unexamined assumption. The first alternative (active enforcement, Option A) was not pursued -- evaluated and explicitly rejected given zero benefit to current behavior and real redesign cost. No planner algorithm, numeric value, or verifier check logic was changed.

The dark VolumeProgressionVerifier reads both fields and can report violations, but it is not wired into CatalogVolumeAndLongRunPlanner or any public generation path. Not enforced by the live planner does not mean not referenced anywhere in the repository; the scoped closure remains CLOSED. risks.title: Live Race-Date Alignment Guard Combines an Exact-12-Week Check with Date Tolerance, Contrary to the Prior Horizon-Agnostic Characterization
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3B RaceDateAlignmentVerifier work, governance follow-up pass (2026-07-24)
risks.source: backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/PreviewRouting/CatalogPreviewGenerator.cs (method BuildDarkInternalDatedSkeleton, the defensive race-date-alignment block; symbol CatalogRaceDateAlignmentInvalidException); backend/RunningApp.Application/Common/RaceHorizonPolicy.cs (ExactStandaloneCoreSupportedWeeks, Classify); backend/RunningApp.Application/Services/PlanServices.cs (upstream horizon gate); backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/Materialization/RaceDateAlignmentVerifier.cs and its test suite; PHASE4G_3A_EIGHT_WEEK_CORE_ALLOCATION_AUDIT.md section 15 (original claim) and its correction addendum
risks.statement: CatalogPreviewGenerator's live CatalogRaceDateAlignmentInvalidException guard (in BuildDarkInternalDatedSkeleton) combines an exact standalone-core week-count check with the race-date tolerance check in a single OR condition: it throws if datedSkeleton.Weeks.Count != RaceHorizonPolicy.ExactStandaloneCoreSupportedWeeks (currently 12), OR daysBeforeRace < 0, OR daysBeforeRace > 7, where daysBeforeRace = RaceDate.DayNumber - datedSkeleton.EndDate.DayNumber. The date component alone accepts a final session when 0 <= RaceDate - FinalSessionDate <= 7 days. The standalone RaceDateAlignmentVerifier independently confirmed, via its own test suite against the real generated 8-14-week TEN_K_MASTER v6 schedules, that this date-tolerance rule succeeds on its own merits for every one of those week counts (FinalSessionDate = RaceDate - 1 in every case). However, the combined live guard would nevertheless reject every one of those non-12-week schedules today purely because of the Weeks.Count clause, even though their dates are correctly aligned. risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.4C.0, sourced from CROSS_PHASE_4G_4A_TO_4G_4B_V_AND_BACKEND_BASELINE_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md's independent adversarial source trace (2026-07-27)
risks.statement: CROSS_PHASE_4G_4A_TO_4G_4B_V_AND_BACKEND_BASELINE_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md independently found, via a source-level adversarial trace performed in that pass (not by re-running Phase 4G.4B's own test suite), that PreparationRunwayValidators only checks CompositionType-vs-RunwayDays internal consistency when Status == NotApplicable: PreparationRunwayPlanningResultValidator's cross-check at that status is the only place any validator compares RacePlanCompositionMetadata.CompositionType against RunwayDays/FullRunwayWeeks. A PreparationRunwayPlanningResult with Status == DecisionRequired, Unsupported, or InvalidInput could therefore carry self-contradictory composition metadata -- for example a CompositionType of StandaloneCore paired with a nonzero RunwayDays value, or a CompositionType of PreparationRunwayPlusCore paired with RunwayDays == 0 -- without any validator catching it. Currently non-blocking: PreparationRunwayContracts/PreparationRunwayValidators are entirely dark and unwired to any live path, per Phase 4G.4B/4G.4B.V's own confirmed scope (zero production call sites outside the dedicated contract folder, no DI registration, no endpoint, no public DTO). This becomes a real risk the moment a future phase (4G.4C or later) begins constructing PreparationRunwayPlanningResult instances from real allocator logic and consumes their Status/metadata without independently re-validating consistency.
affectedAreas: PreparationRunwayContextValidator / RacePlanCompositionMetadataValidator / PreparationRunwayPlanningResultValidator
RacePlanCompositionType / PreparationRunwayPlanningStatus consistency enforcement
Any future Preparation Runway allocator (Phase 4G.4C or later) that constructs and consumes PreparationRunwayPlanningResult instances
requiredResolution: Before Phase 4G.4C (or whichever phase first implements a runway allocator that produces real PreparationRunwayPlanningResult instances) is considered complete, extend PreparationRunwayValidators to enforce CompositionType/RunwayDays consistency across ALL statuses, not only NotApplicable -- or explicitly document, with reasoning, why the other statuses are exempt if that turns out to be intentional.
Cross-reference CROSS_PHASE_4G_4A_TO_4G_4B_V_AND_BACKEND_BASELINE_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md section 6 as the source of this finding when this risk is next revisited.

risks.closureNote: Resolution (Phase 4G.4B.1): PreparationRunwayContextValidator.Validate now enforces a general, status-independent CompositionType/RunwayDays consistency rule -- CompositionType==PreparationRunwayPlusCore requires RunwayDays > 0, and any other CompositionType requires RunwayDays == 0 -- matching the exact binary convention every existing test helper (Context()/Metadata() in PreparationRunwayContractsTests.cs) already used to construct consistent inputs. Because RacePlanCompositionMetadataValidator.Validate (which builds a context from this rule) is called unconditionally by PreparationRunwayPlanningResultValidator.Validate for every Status, this single check now applies identically to Planned, DecisionRequired, Unsupported, InvalidInput, and NotApplicable alike -- closing the gap without any status-specific duplication. The pre-existing NotApplicable-specific check (which additionally forbids NotApplicable from claiming an allocation) was left untouched and re-confirmed still passing. New tests reproduce the audit's own literal adversarial example (CompositionType=StandaloneCore with RunwayDays=7, wrapped in a DecisionRequired result) plus the same mismatch under Unsupported and InvalidInput, plus the reverse-direction mismatch (PreparationRunwayPlusCore with RunwayDays==0) -- all now correctly rejected. No allocator, materializer, composer, or live-path code was touched; PreparationRunwayContracts/PreparationRunwayValidators remain entirely dark per Phase 4G.4B/4G.4B.V's own confirmed scope, re-verified unchanged by this fix.
risks.closureCriteriaSatisfied: First requiredResolution option's first alternative fully satisfied: PreparationRunwayValidators now enforces CompositionType/RunwayDays consistency across ALL statuses, not only NotApplicable, via a single general check rather than per-status duplication. risks.statement: A repo-wide grep for CoreHorizonDecision and CoreHorizonMode usage outside CoreHorizonClassifier.cs's own file found zero production references, including inside CatalogPhaseAllocation.cs (the real CatalogPhaseAllocationResolver.Resolve phase-week-count allocator). risks.closureNote: Phase 4I.2A approved: RecoveryWeekTotalVolumeKm = Round_0.5km(max(PreviousDevelopmentPeakVolumeKm x (1 - 0.15), PreviousDevelopmentPeakVolumeKm - 0.5km-guaranteed-minimum-drop)), where PreviousDevelopmentPeakVolumeKm is the mesocycle's Week-3 (highest-load) volume, per progression_rules_v2.yaml's cutbackPolicy.reductionRatioByProfile.INTERMEDIATE=[0.15,0.20] -- 0.15 (the conservative/minimum bound of the explicit canonical range) selected per this phase's own decision standard (explicit range; conservative point; compatible with existing 0.07/0.08/2.5km caps; safe under 0.5km rounding; no transition discontinuity; product-default status recorded). RecoveryWeekLongRunKm = Round_0.5km(RecoveryWeekTotalVolumeKm x 0.33) -- reusing VolumeSafetyPolicy.Default's existing LongRunSelectionShare unmodified, guaranteeing the long-run share never rises and the recovery long run is always lower than the preceding development week's long run (same share, smaller base). KEY_SESSION/EASY_SUPPORT/LONG_RUN distance split reuses FourDaySessionDistanceAllocationPolicy.Allocate unmodified -- no new session-level formula. Feasibility: if the resulting week cannot satisfy the existing MinimumKeySessionDistanceKm(3)+2xMinimumEasySupportDistanceKm(1.5) residual floor, materialization must fail closed (reusing the existing CatalogSessionPrescriptionInfeasibleException mechanism), never silently violate the minimum or silently skip the reduction. Both CONSISTENCY_NEEDED and CORE_ENTRY_READY use the IDENTICAL 0.15 ratio and reference week -- progression_rules_v2.yaml's profile axis is EXPERIENCE LEVEL (NEW/INTERMEDIATE/ADVANCED/EXPERIENCED), not the GE readiness-profile axis, and the current pilot's both readiness profiles map to the single INTERMEDIATE experience level; profile differences remain confined to KEY_SESSION content selection (Phase 4I.2's own architecture), never numeric magnitude. Return-from-recovery reuses progression_rules_v2.yaml's postCutbackProgressionBaseline=PREVIOUS_NON_CUTBACK_VOLUME verbatim: the next development week's 0.07/0.08/2.5km progression caps apply relative to the PRE-recovery mesocycle peak, not the recovery week's reduced value -- preventing sawtooth re-growth-from-a-deconditioned-baseline across up to 8 mesocycles (32 weeks). Terminal interaction: a FullPhase duration that is an exact multiple of 4 (e.g. 4, 8, 12, ...) does end its GE segment on a Recovery week immediately before Runway -- accepted, not treated as a defect, because Phase 4I.2's own approved GE-to-Runway continuity rule (final GE aligns UPWARD toward Runway, Runway Week 1's approved 8-week structure remains unchanged) already bridges a reduced final week into Runway Week 1 without requiring a new terminal exception; for non-multiple-of-4 remainders, the terminal 1-3 weeks are Alignment (never Recovery, per Phase 4I.2), so a real Recovery week is never immediately adjacent to Runway in those cases. Recovery is explicitly distinguished from Taper: Taper is a race-proximity, performance-peaking, single-occurrence reduction (TaperVolumeMultiplier=0.53, applied once, never recurring); Recovery is a repeating, phase-interior, fitness-maintaining reduction recurring every 4 weeks throughout GE -- the two numeric magnitudes are NOT interchangeable and this decision does not borrow Taper's 0.53 value. Evidence classification: A/B (a real, precedence-level-2 canonical rule file, already cited as an accepted source in an unrelated prior audit entry, self-declared evidenceLevel=EVIDENCE_INFORMED with unresolvable-within-repository source labels S2/S6 -- not upgraded to EVIDENCE_BACKED). Explicit non-claims: this ratio is not claimed to prevent injury; it is not claimed to be laboratory-validated; it is a conservative, already-canonical, previously-unwired product default extended one segment (BUILD/RACE_SPECIFIC to GE) via the classification-D generalization already used repeatedly throughout Phase 4I.1/4I.2 for other reused constants. Final classification: LONG_HORIZON_GENERAL_ENDURANCE_NUMERIC_RECOVERY_POLICY_APPROVED. Runtime activation remains fully blocked regardless, unchanged, under TD-GENERAL-ENDURANCE-STAGED-PLAN-001 (still OPEN -- this decision closes only the numeric-policy gap, not rolling materialization, segment-provenance persistence, transition orchestration, or catalog content). GE-to-Runway catalog compatibility: the final GE week's KEY_SESSION resolves to EASY_STANDARD (family EASY), structurally compatible with the Preparation Runway's own Consistency-Step-1 opening reference (also EASY_STANDARD) -- no prohibited-intensity jump, no duplicate transition semantics; numeric continuity (volume/pace) is explicitly and entirely deferred to a later phase, not computed here. risks.title: Runway Semantic Role and Structural Decisions Resolved for GE-Exit-Above-Core-Target State; Exact Numeric Convergence Formula Remains an Explicit, Evidence-Backed Open Gap -- Not Invented
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4I.6B -- Long-Horizon Runway Entry-Above-Core-Target Numeric Transition Policy Resolution (2026-08-02), a pure governance/policy-decision pass -- zero production code changed.
risks.source: Repository-wide review of PreparationRunwayStartingLoadEvidence, PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer, VolumeSafetyPolicy.Default, progression_rules_v2.yaml cutbackPolicy, TenKPreparationRunwayDarkOrchestrator, and Phase 4I.6A's own discovered failure; new real-evidence diagnostic (backend/RunningApp.IntegrationTests/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/LongHorizonRunwayEntryAboveCoreTargetPolicyDiagnosticTests.cs, 3 tests) empirically measuring the real GE-exit-vs-Core-Week-1-target gap for the documented 28/40/52-week failing cases using the exact real, unchanged GE numeric executor and Core generation pipeline (typical baseline: 20km/8km recent evidence).
affectedAreas: Future Phase 4I.6C runtime implementation, which remains blocked on the unresolved numeric magnitude question
Possible future governance review of GE's own uncapped multi-mesocycle compounding growth for very long horizons (a related but explicitly out-of-scope finding, see closureNote)
requiredResolution: RESOLVED (structural, Class D architecture-consistency, no invented numeric value): Runway's semantic role in this state is 'entry consolidation at the Core target' -- distinct from GE recovery (single interior week, 0.85 policy), Taper (race-proximity, single occurrence, 0.53 policy), and normal upward Runway progression. The GE-side-ceiling candidate (capping GE progression by the future Core target) is REJECTED: it would make an earlier general-development phase dependent on a later phase-specific target, contradicting Phase 4I.2's approved independent-development semantics, and is explicitly out of this phase's scope to redesign. The Core-target-lifting candidate (raising Core Week 1 from incoming Runway load) is REJECTED: Core's target is evidence-derived from the runner's own declared baseline, independent of any preceding segment, and lifting it would require re-deriving Core's own numeric decision, contradicting 'do not change Core algorithms.' Workout identity and pace/intensity semantics are unaffected in either case (only the volume/distance trajectory is in question). The policy applies to both readiness profiles identically (no evidence supports profile-specific numeric branching); it is a strictly additive third transition mode, never altering existing 15-20 week behavior or GE-exit-at-or-below-target behavior.

NOT RESOLVED (the actual numeric gap): real diagnostic evidence shows the excess magnitude scales steeply and unboundedly with horizon length under the existing, unmodified GE progression policy alone (28 weeks: ~4km excess; 40 weeks: ~21.5km excess; 52 weeks: ~41km excess, against a fixed ~20km Core target -- i.e. GE's own peak reaches ~71.5km/week by week 52, over 3x the Core target). No canonical rule, approved product default, generalizable existing production behavior, or strong domain evidence exists in this repository for a specific multi-week (non-recovery, non-Taper) weekly-reduction magnitude capable of safely bridging gaps of this size within a fixed 8-week Runway. The existing 0.07/0.08 increase ratios, 2.5km absolute cap, 0.85 recovery ratio, and 0.53 Taper multiplier are each evidenced for a DIFFERENT semantic purpose and this phase's own explicit instruction forbids reusing any of them for this purpose without direct, independent support -- none was found. An 'immediate ceiling clamp' (Runway entry = Core target, zero new formula, existing upward-progression algorithm proceeds unchanged) was evaluated as the only formula-free candidate, but is REJECTED as an approved default for large excesses (40/52-week cases): a single-step 65%+ volume drop is exactly the 'hidden Taper' / 'unnecessary detraining' risk this phase's own decision standard requires rejecting without real evidence it is safe. It remains a plausible candidate only for small excesses (~28-week case, ~17% relative excess) but selecting even that narrower scope as a blanket 'default' would still be inventing an unevidenced magnitude threshold -- not approved.

This TD must remain OPEN. Phase 4I.6C (approved-policy runtime implementation) cannot proceed as unblocked; see TD-GENERAL-ENDURANCE-STAGED-PLAN-001 for the umbrella tracking entry. A future phase should consider, as a SEPARATE governance question, whether GE's own uncapped compounding growth for very long horizons (not the Runway transition) is the more foundational issue worth resolving first.

risks.closureNote: Phase 4I.6B.1 ran the real, unchanged production pipeline (real GE numeric executor, real horizon-invariant Core Week-1 target measurement, real RuntimeConditionResolutionService) across all 32 horizons (21-52) x 2 readiness profiles x 3 approved input classes (Low=15km/5km, Typical=20km/8km, High=30km/12km recent-weekly-volume/longest-run) -- 192 combinations. Key structural finding: the Core Week-1 target equals the raw RecentWeeklyVolumeKm evidence value directly (confirmed horizon-invariant and unclamped for all tested magnitudes), which also equals GE's own Week-1 entry value by construction -- meaning ANY GE development-progression growth beyond week 1 immediately creates a nonzero entry-above-target excess. Real results: 21 total weeks (GE=1, no progression) PASSES for every class/profile with zero excess; 22 and 23 total weeks (GE=2/3, mid-mesocycle upward progression) FAIL for every class/profile; 24 total weeks (GE=4, which lands exactly on a GE recovery week) PASSES again for every class/profile -- a real, confirmed, non-monotonic 'isolated later success' caused by GE's own approved recovery formula coincidentally landing on the horizon's final week; every horizon 25-52 FAILS for every tested class/profile (confirming Phase 4I.6B's own finding that failure becomes the norm, not the exception, for longer horizons). Per this phase's own explicit instruction against activating isolated later successes, the correct answer is the longest CONTIGUOUS universally-supported prefix starting at 21, which is exactly {21} -- MaxNumericallySupportedTotalWeeks = 21, FirstNumericallyInactiveTotalWeeks = 22. This was confirmed end-to-end (not just via the GE-exit-vs-Core-target comparison) by running the real LongHorizonFullNumericOrchestrator for 21 (succeeds), 22 (throws the existing, unmodified Runway 'no approved non-taper runway reduction rule exists' exception), and 24 (succeeds, confirming the real pipeline agrees with the comparison-based prediction exactly). Technical maximum = recommended product maximum = 21 (no rationale exists to recommend against activating a horizon that is proven safe by the full matrix). Path B is adopted per this phase's own product direction: the 21-52 week COMPOSITION policy (Phase 4I.1) is entirely preserved and unchanged -- GE/Runway/Core durations, GE catalog capacity (Phase 4I.4), and structural materialization (Phase 4I.5) all remain valid and unmodified for every horizon 21-52. Only NUMERIC RUNTIME ACTIVATION is narrowed. 22-52 weeks are explicitly NOT reclassified as exceeding the supported composition window (that remains exclusively the 53+ PLAN_HORIZON_EXCEEDS_SUPPORTED_WINDOW reason, unchanged) -- a new, distinct conceptual reason (LONG_HORIZON_NUMERIC_ENVELOPE_NOT_SUPPORTED) is defined for the 22-52 week composition-eligible-but-numerically-inactive state, though its production implementation remains for a future phase. No convergence percentage, GE ceiling, or Core-target lifting was introduced -- this phase changed zero production code. Non-claims: this decision does not claim 21 weeks is a product-meaningful Long-Horizon offering on its own (GE=1 week involves no meaningful development), only that it is the sole horizon the current numeric pipeline can support without inventing anything; it does not claim the 22-52 week range is permanently unsupportable, only that it is inactive under the CURRENT numeric model pending Path A. Final classification: LONG_HORIZON_NUMERIC_ACTIVATION_BOUNDARY_APPROVED_WITH_STRUCTURAL_21_TO_52_SUPPORT_PRESERVED_AND_RUNTIME_NUMERIC_ACTIVATION_LIMITED_TO_21_THROUGH_21. See PHASE4I_6B_1_SUPPORTED_LONG_HORIZON_NUMERIC_BOUNDARY_RESOLUTION.md for the full record and PHASE4I_6B_1_HORIZON_SCAN_MATRIX.csv for the complete 193-row machine-readable matrix.

risks.closureNote: Phase 4K.2 approved: (1) EVIDENCE WINDOW -- the most recent activated numeric window (up to 4 weeks; fewer when a partial GE window was activated), sourced exclusively from TrainingDay.ActualDistanceKm for sessions with Status=Completed; Missed/Skipped/SoftMissed sessions (including NotTodayDecision's default ResultingStatus=Missed) count as ZERO actual distance within the week -- never excluded from the denominator and never inferred from PlannedDistanceKm -- keeping the aggregate conservative rather than inflated. (2) VALIDATED WEEKLY LOAD -- ValidatedSustainableWeeklyVolumeKm = mean of ACTUAL summed weekly distance across the non-recovery weeks of the evidence window (candidate B), rounded via the existing VolumeSafetyPolicy.Default 0.5km increment. The recovery/consolidation week is EXCLUDED from the average (its planned reduction is by design, not a completion failure) but its own actual completion still counts toward adherence; the pre-recovery planned peak is NEVER automatically assumed achieved without its own completed evidence -- no artificial upward inflation. For ShortExtension partial windows (1-3 GE weeks, structurally never containing a recovery week per Phase 4I.2) the full available window is used directly. (3) VALIDATED LONG-RUN LOAD -- ValidatedSustainableLongRunKm = mean of completed LONG_RUN ActualDistanceKm across the same non-recovery evidence weeks, additionally bounded by the EXISTING LongRunHardCapShare(0.40)-of-weekly-volume ceiling -- a single anomalously long completed run can never independently define the next block's long run, since it is always averaged with, and capped relative to, the validated weekly volume. Zero completed long runs in the window with no usable prior evidence contributes to VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE (Blocked). (4) ADHERENCE ROLE -- the EXISTING AdherenceRatePercent (completedRuns/totalRuns*100) is reused verbatim as a Growth-eligibility CONFIDENCE gate (evidence is 'sufficient' or not), NOT folded numerically into the weekly-load average (which already reflects incompletion via zero-counted misses) and NOT weighted differently by role (Easy/Key/Long treated uniformly, no evidence supports differential weighting); NotToday and unexplained misses are treated identically for this numeric purpose. No exact adherence threshold is invented -- deferred to Phase 4K.3 as an explicit, disclosed blocker, per the phase's own explicit instruction against inventing an unsupported percentage. (5) GROWTH ELIGIBLE -- requires: validated weekly load exists; validated long-run evidence exists; adherence is sufficient (exact threshold deferred); no unresolved safety conflict (taxonomy deferred); four viable sessions producible from the validated load (reusing FourDaySessionDistanceAllocationPolicy's existing feasibility check unchanged); next progression via the EXISTING GE development-progression authority (0.07/0.08 ratio, 2.5km absolute cap) remains inside the existing peak-volume band. GrowthEligible does NOT mean an increase is mandatory -- the existing authority may still produce zero delta from caps/rounding/stage semantics; no second progression formula was created. (6) MAINTENANCE ONLY -- selected when evidence exists but does not support Growth, OR no new evidence exists but a PRIOR validated sustainable load remains usable, provided no safety-critical/infeasibility/missing-load condition applies -- maintenance is explicitly NOT a fallback for invalid inputs, unresolved safety signals, four-session infeasibility, total absence of validated load evidence, or an unsupported segment transition; all of those fail closed instead (Blocked). (7) MAINTENANCE ANCHOR -- MaintenanceAnchorWeeklyVolumeKm = ValidatedSustainableWeeklyVolumeKm directly (the actual completed average), subject to existing rounding/peak-band/session-feasibility rules -- explicitly NOT a percentage of original baseline, planned peak, Core Week-1 target, GE recovery volume, or the 0.53 Taper multiplier; the anchor never exceeds the last validated completed average (actual evidence always takes precedence over any previously planned-but-unevidenced target). (8) FOUR-WEEK MAINTENANCE SHAPE -- Weeks 1-3 are flat at the maintenance anchor (only long-run-share/rounding-driven micro-variance, never a real change); Week 4 reuses the EXISTING 0.85 recovery formula (Phase 4I.2A, unmodified) applied to the maintenance anchor as its own PREVIOUS_NON_CUTBACK_VOLUME-equivalent reference (since no growth occurred, the anchor itself is this mesocycle's peak-equivalent); no maintenance week may produce a new planned weekly-volume peak; the recovery formula itself is not redefined. (9) MAINTENANCE LONG-RUN ENVELOPE -- reuses the EXISTING long-run-share rule (0.33 selection share, clamped to [0.30, min(0.36,0.40)]) applied to the flat maintenance anchor -- because the anchor does not grow, the derived long run algebraically cannot produce a new peak either, with zero new share/constant invented; Week 4's long run reuses the existing 0.33-of-recovery-total rule unchanged. (10) CONSECUTIVE MAINTENANCE WINDOWS -- approved: multiple MaintenanceOnly windows may occur back-to-back when new evidence continues not to support Growth but a validated sustainable load remains available and safe; the anchor is REFRESHED each window from that window's own actual completed evidence (never inherited unchanged), preventing both automatic upward drift and repeated recovery-week-averaging decline (since recovery weeks are always excluded from the average, per (2)); exact evidence-age/staleness rules are deferred to Phase 4K.3; the Runway segment boundary always takes precedence when reached. (11) PARTIAL WINDOWS -- the Growth/Maintenance decision applies only to the remaining GE portion of a partial window; when a window crosses from GE into Runway, Runway weeks are governed exclusively by the EXISTING, unmodified Runway numeric authority (Phase 4I.6A) -- GE maintenance rules are never applied to Runway weeks, and no synthetic recovery week is ever inserted merely to pad a block to four weeks. (12) BLOCKED ACTIVATION -- four reason families approved: VALIDATED_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE, VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, NUMERIC_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE (four-session infeasibility per existing session-minimum rules), SAFETY_REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED (detailed taxonomy deferred to Phase 4K.3) -- never collapsed into one generic reason; maintenance is explicitly confirmed NOT a universal fallback for any of these. Note: a plan's very FIRST numeric window continues to use the existing, unmodified Phase 4I.6 onboarding-evidence baseline mechanism, not this checkpoint policy, which applies to SUBSEQUENT windows. (13) ROUNDING -- reuses the existing 0.5km increment and existing session-distribution policy unchanged; raw actual evidence is always aggregated BEFORE rounding/progression is applied; no new rounding increment was introduced. (14) PROFILE POLICY -- identical validated-load formula, Growth/Maintenance eligibility, and maintenance anchor for both CONSISTENCY_NEEDED and CORE_ENTRY_READY; profile differences remain confined to workout content selection, matching every prior phase's finding. (15) NON-CLAIMS recorded verbatim: validated sustainable load is a product decision metric, not a laboratory fitness measurement; completed volume does not prove injury safety; maintenance does not guarantee fitness preservation; no universal adherence percentage is claimed; no universal weekly-volume increase rule is introduced; maintenance is not Taper; maintenance is not GE recovery; pain/medical symptoms require separate safety handling (deferred); wearable/HRV data is not required. Zero maintenance PERCENTAGE, zero adherence THRESHOLD, and zero production code were introduced -- only the existing 0.85/0.33/0.5km/0.07/0.08/2.5km constants already approved elsewhere are reused, and the maintenance anchor is defined structurally (=validated load) rather than as any new ratio. Final classification: LONG_HORIZON_VALIDATED_LOAD_GROWTH_ELIGIBILITY_AND_MAINTENANCE_ENVELOPE_POLICY_APPROVED. See PHASE4K_2_VALIDATED_LOAD_GROWTH_ELIGIBILITY_AND_MAINTENANCE_ENVELOPE_POLICY_RESOLUTION.md for the full record.

risks.closureNote: Phase 4K.1 approved, as an explicit, typed, high-level product-lifecycle policy (Path A's actual shape, replacing the rejected Path B one-horizon model): (1) STRUCTURAL VS NUMERIC SPLIT -- a confirmed Long-Horizon plan always contains a complete structural roadmap for all 21-52 weeks (segment/stage/week/workout-role structure, dates where already structurally known -- Phase 4I.1/4I.4/4I.5 unchanged) but numeric prescription (executable distance/long-run/pace/effort/intensity) is limited to a bounded near-term ACTIVATION WINDOW, recalculated from current validated evidence rather than generated once from initial evidence. (2) ACTIVATION WINDOW = 4 weeks, an explicit Appsel PRODUCT DEFAULT (not a universal physiological rule) chosen because it exactly matches the already-approved GE 3-development+1-recovery mesocycle (Phase 4I.2) -- one complete numeric unit, avoiding mesocycle-splitting. Applies to both the initial window and every subsequent window. Partial windows ARE allowed at segment boundaries: a ShortExtension GE segment (1-3 weeks) activates only its own remaining GE weeks; when fewer than 4 GE weeks remain before the Runway boundary, the window MAY extend into the immediately following Runway weeks (reusing the existing, real, already-authoritative Runway pipeline as a valid activation target, avoiding an artificially short 1-3 week orphan window) rather than truncating or padding. (3) LIFECYCLE STATES -- exactly six approved: StructurallyPlanned, NumericPending, NumericActivated, Completed, Missed, NumericActivationBlocked. Structurally-planned/pending future weeks carry null (never fabricated zero) distance/duration/pace fields; only activated weeks carry complete executable prescriptions; completed/missed weeks are immutable history, never rewritten; only future, not-yet-started weeks may receive new numeric activation; structural segment identity (segment/stage/globally-numbered week) remains stable across every recalculation. (4) CHECKPOINT AUTHORITY -- a checkpoint evaluates current evidence and returns a typed decision (permit progression / require maintenance / block upward progression / block activation entirely) that is AUTHORITATIVE for activating the NEXT numeric window only; it never rewrites completed history and never changes the approved structural roadmap by default. Detailed evidence fields/aggregation/thresholds are explicitly deferred to Phase 4K.3, not decided here. (5) MISSING-EVIDENCE PRINCIPLE -- 'no new validated evidence implies no upward numeric progression' is approved as the minimum safety rule; a maintenance-only window MAY be permitted if the last validated sustainable load and all minimum safety inputs remain available, otherwise the pipeline fails closed (blocks activation) -- the exact maintenance anchor/formula is explicitly deferred to Phase 4K.2, not decided here. (6) STRUCTURAL IMMUTABILITY -- race date, total structural horizon, GE/Runway/Core composition, segment order, global week numbering, completed history, and catalog provenance all remain stable/immutable after confirmation; future numeric activation is explicitly NOT treated as retroactive structural mutation. (7) RUNWAY/CORE JUST-IN-TIME PRINCIPLE -- Runway and Core remain structurally present from plan creation, but their final numeric prescriptions are resolved using CURRENT validated evidence near their own activation boundary (not frozen from initial-creation evidence, which may be many months stale by the time a 21-52 week plan reaches its Runway/Core segments); the existing real Runway/Core pipelines, target-time/goal-feasibility/pace-source policies all remain fully unchanged and authoritative; no Core target is ever arbitrarily lifted from planned GE progression (reaffirming Phase 4I.6B's own rejection), and no GE-side ceiling is introduced. Exact JIT checkpoint timing and evidence precedence are explicitly deferred to Phase 4K.4. (8) PUBLIC PRODUCT SEMANTICS (conceptual only, no DTO field names decided) -- a confirmed plan conceptually contains: the complete structural roadmap, the currently activated numeric window, future numeric-pending weeks (never appearing as executable prescriptions before activation), next-checkpoint information, and numeric lifecycle status; the user-facing principle is 'Appsel shows the full journey; only the near-term prescription is finalized; later prescriptions are recalculated from updated evidence' -- explicitly not 'your plan is incomplete' framing. (9) NON-CLAIMS recorded verbatim: four weeks is a product default, not a universal physiological rule; rolling activation does not guarantee injury prevention; maintenance is not Taper; checkpoint reassessment is not medical diagnosis; planned progression is not proof of achieved fitness; future Core capacity cannot be inferred solely from the original baseline; HRV/wearable data is not required by this decision. This decision approves the SHAPE of the solution only -- zero maintenance formula, zero checkpoint evidence threshold, zero Runway/Core timing rule, and zero production/contract/persistence/API/Flutter code were introduced or implied. Final classification: LONG_HORIZON_ROLLING_NUMERIC_ACTIVATION_AND_REASSESSMENT_AUTHORITY_POLICY_APPROVED. See PHASE4K_1_LONG_HORIZON_ROLLING_NUMERIC_ACTIVATION_AND_REASSESSMENT_AUTHORITY_POLICY_RESOLUTION.md for the full record.

risks.closureNote: Phase 4K.3 approved: (1) EVIDENCE SNAPSHOT -- the checkpoint evidence snapshot is a conceptual, policy-only field set (checkpointDate, activatedWindowStartWeek/EndWeek, completedWindowWeeks, actualWeeklyVolumes, completedLongRuns, completedRunsCount, plannedRunsCount, AdherenceRatePercent, missedSessionCount, current-availability signal, safety/pain signal, prior validated sustainable weekly load and long run, current segment, weeks until Runway) that distinguishes evidence observed in the current window from previously validated evidence, from original onboarding evidence, and from structurally planned future values; future planned values (null per Phase 4K.1) NEVER enter the snapshot -- only actual, already-realized TrainingDay outcomes do. (2) WEEKLY-VOLUME FRESHNESS -- the expected source window is the most recent activated four-week block (Phase 4K.1's activation window; fewer weeks for a partial GE window); older completed weeks from a PRIOR activated block may NOT fill missing positions in the current window (that would silently blend two evidence generations) -- if the current block is incomplete, it is either used as-is (Growth confidence permitting, see (6)) or the prior block's own validated load is used in full as a Maintenance anchor (never a blend); the maximum age before evidence is considered stale is the length of the activation window itself (4 weeks), an explicit Appsel PRODUCT DEFAULT since no existing repository rule addresses weekly-volume evidence age (the only existing age rule, PaceSourceResolver's 30/60/90/180-day ladder, is scoped exclusively to race-pace evidence and is explicitly NOT reused for weekly volume, a different evidence type). (3) LONG-RUN FRESHNESS -- reuses the SAME 4-week activation-window freshness rule as weekly-volume evidence (not the unrelated 30-day race-pace ladder); the most recent activated block is sufficient; when no completed long run exists within the fresh window, per Phase 4K.2's VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE this phase confirms NO safe bounded-long-run substitute is defined -- the default is NumericActivationBlocked, not MaintenanceOnly, because Phase 4K.2 did not approve any such substitute and inventing one now would exceed this phase's scope. (4) ADHERENCE FRESHNESS -- AdherenceRatePercent for checkpoint purposes MUST be computed over the most recent activated block only and MUST NOT be inherited indefinitely from older blocks; a stale block's adherence value cannot satisfy a later checkpoint. (5) AVAILABILITY AND SAFETY FRESHNESS -- PreferredDays/availability remain structurally stored but do not by themselves prove current availability; absent an explicit conflicting signal (no availability-confirmation mechanism exists in the repository today), current availability is presumptively treated as unchanged for both Growth and Maintenance -- the exact confirmation UX/contract is out of scope for this policy phase. An unresolved safety-critical signal NEVER expires automatically -- it fails closed (blocks activation) until explicitly resolved by a future, separate safety-review mechanism; non-safety difficulty/fatigue signals are not defined by this phase (no structured taxonomy exists in the repository beyond the free-text InjuryNotes field and the unimplemented SafetyValidatorBlocked key) and therefore cannot yet restrict Growth beyond the safety-critical case. (6) TERMINAL-WINDOW RULE -- a checkpoint may issue a next-window decision only when the activated window's calendar period has ended AND every planned session has reached a terminal outcome (Completed, Missed, Skipped, or SoftMissed -- PendingConfirmation and the never-assigned Rescheduled value are explicitly non-terminal); unresolved sessions are NEVER silently counted as zero or Completed. If the window is not yet terminal, the checkpoint issues NO next-window Growth decision; it may still issue MaintenanceOnly using ONLY a prior validated anchor (never the incomplete current window's partial data) when a prior anchor remains available and safety is clear, reason CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_NOT_COMPLETE; otherwise it is NumericActivationBlocked with the same reason. Partial segment-boundary (ShortExtension) windows use the identical terminal rule scoped to their own, shorter set of planned sessions. (7) PARTIAL COMPLETION -- TrainingDayStatus has no distinct 'partial' value; a session completed with less than its planned distance is still Status=Completed and its actual (lower) ActualDistanceKm naturally and sufficiently lowers the Phase 4K.2 weekly/long-run averages -- no separate percentage-complete threshold is invented, and no additional partial-completion bookkeeping is introduced beyond what Phase 4K.2's mean-of-actuals formula already produces. Repeated partial completions are self-correcting through the load average itself and through condition (9)'s per-week evidence check -- they do not silently unlock Growth. (8) MISSED AND NOT-TODAY TREATMENT -- Missed contributes zero actual distance and lowers adherence, exactly as Phase 4K.2 already established; NotToday-resolved sessions (default ResultingStatus=Missed) are treated IDENTICALLY to unexplained Missed sessions for numeric purposes, per Phase 4K.2's own closure. TrainingDayStatus.Rescheduled is confirmed reserved-but-unimplemented in the current repository (never assigned anywhere) -- this phase documents, for any future implementer, that a Rescheduled session must be treated as non-terminal (like PendingConfirmation) until it resolves to a genuine terminal status; it must never be auto-treated as Completed. An unexplained unresolved session (no terminal status and no NotTodayDecision) after the calendar period has ended blocks the checkpoint per (6). Multiple misses NEVER directly force MaintenanceOnly or Blocked on their own -- they operate exclusively through the already-defined validated-load-availability (Phase 4K.2) and Growth-confidence (9) channels; no new role-specific or count-based miss weighting is invented. (9) ADHERENCE CONFIDENCE GATE -- no accepted numeric adherence threshold exists anywhere in the repository (confirmed by exhaustive search), and per this phase's own explicit instruction no new percentage is invented. The approved, deterministic, non-percentage GROWTH CONFIDENCE CONDITION is: every non-recovery week of the activated window contains at least one Completed session with usable actual evidence (the window's terminal-window rule from (6) must also hold). The approved MAINTENANCE CONFIDENCE CONDITION is: a validated sustainable weekly load is available -- from the current window if (6) holds but the Growth condition above does not, or from a prior fresh-enough window if the current window has no usable evidence -- and no safety/feasibility conflict exists. The approved BLOCKED CONFIDENCE CONDITION is: no validated load is available from either the current or any prior fresh window. If the Growth confidence condition cannot be met, Growth is blocked for that checkpoint and MaintenanceOnly is evaluated instead under its own, separate condition -- Growth is never silently defaulted to, and Maintenance is never treated as an automatic consequence of failing Growth without its own validated-load check. (10) SAFETY AND PAIN SIGNALS -- the repository contains no structured pain/injury/difficulty taxonomy (only TrainingPlan.InjuryNotes free text and the unimplemented SafetyValidatorBlocked key); this phase invents no medical-scoring system. The approved high-level rule: an unresolved safety-critical signal (once a future mechanism can produce one) ALWAYS produces NumericActivationBlocked with reason SAFETY_REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED, evaluated with the highest priority in the transition table (10a), before any other condition -- it can never produce GrowthEligible, and this phase does not approve it silently downgrading to MaintenanceOnly either, since an unresolved safety concern is not equivalent to an ordinary evidence gap. Non-safety difficulty/fatigue signals are explicitly out of scope (no repository policy exists to draw that distinction yet). (11) EVIDENCE SUFFICIENCY -- Growth requires: terminal window (6); validated weekly load AND validated long-run evidence available from the CURRENT window (2)(3); Growth confidence condition (9); safety clear (10); four-session feasibility via the existing, unmodified FourDaySessionDistanceAllocationPolicy.Allocate (throws CatalogSessionPrescriptionInfeasibleException on infeasibility). Maintenance requires: a validated weekly load available from the current OR a prior fresh window; safety clear; feasibility holding for that anchor. Blocked requires any of: no valid current-or-prior load anchor; required long-run evidence unavailable with no approved substitute; feasibility failure; unresolved safety signal; window non-terminal with no usable prior anchor. (12) STATE-TRANSITION TABLE -- eight deterministic, mutually exclusive cases evaluated in this priority order (first match wins, guaranteeing exactly one output): (a) safetyClear=false -> NumericActivationBlocked/SAFETY_REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED; (b) windowTerminal=false and no usable prior anchor -> NumericActivationBlocked/CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_NOT_COMPLETE; (c) windowTerminal=false and a prior anchor is available and safe -> MaintenanceOnly/CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_NOT_COMPLETE (using the prior anchor only); (d) no validated weekly load from current or any prior fresh window -> NumericActivationBlocked/VALIDATED_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE; (e) validated long-run evidence unavailable with no approved substitute -> NumericActivationBlocked/VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE; (f) numericFeasible=false -> NumericActivationBlocked/NUMERIC_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE; (g) all sufficiency conditions hold but the Growth confidence condition (9) fails -> MaintenanceOnly/ADHERENCE_CONFIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_GROWTH (current window) or MaintenanceOnly/CHECKPOINT_EVIDENCE_STALE (prior-window reuse, no new current evidence at all); (h) all conditions including Growth confidence hold -> GrowthEligible/no reason (GrowthEligible never carries a failure reason). (13) REASON TAXONOMY -- exactly nine typed reasons approved: CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_NOT_COMPLETE, CHECKPOINT_EVIDENCE_STALE, VALIDATED_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE, VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, ADHERENCE_CONFIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_GROWTH, MAINTENANCE_ANCHOR_UNAVAILABLE (reserved for a Maintenance anchor that fails its own rounding/peak-band/feasibility re-check after being selected), NUMERIC_WINDOW_INFEASIBLE, SAFETY_REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED, EVIDENCE_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED (reserved for a future case where two evidence sources genuinely disagree in a way this phase does not yet resolve). GrowthEligible carries no failure reason; MaintenanceOnly always carries a non-failure decision-provenance reason explaining why Growth was not selected; Blocked always carries exactly one authoritative reason, never a generic collapse of safety and missing-evidence causes into one code; internal exception wording (e.g. CatalogSessionPrescriptionInfeasibleException's message) is never exposed as the reason code or as product copy. (14) GROWTH DOES NOT MEAN AUTOMATIC INCREASE -- reconfirmed verbatim from Phase 4K.2: GrowthEligible means the existing progression engine (0.07/0.08/2.5km, Phase 4I.2) MAY calculate the next window; it does not mean every week increases, the first week must exceed the maintenance anchor, caps may be bypassed, or a new peak is guaranteed. No progression values are defined by this phase. (15) MAINTENANCE TRANSITION AND SEGMENT-BOUNDARY AUTHORITY -- MaintenanceOnly always uses the Phase 4K.2 anchor/shape/Week-4-recovery rules unchanged; a next checkpoint always still occurs; consecutive maintenance windows are allowed (Phase 4K.2); Maintenance never permanently downgrades the structural roadmap. The checkpoint state decision governs ONLY the remaining GE portion of a window -- ordinary GE Growth/Maintenance logic NEVER prescribes Runway or Core weeks; ordinary next-GE-window checkpoint behavior is overridden the moment a Runway segment boundary is reached, at which point Runway/Core's existing just-in-time authority (Phase 4K.1 principle) takes over; if that JIT context is unavailable at the boundary, activation becomes NumericActivationBlocked, but the exact reason code and evidence precedence for that specific boundary case are explicitly deferred to Phase 4K.4, since resolving it requires JIT-specific evidence this phase does not define. (16) INITIAL WINDOW -- the plan's very first numeric window uses the existing, unmodified Phase 4I.6 onboarding-evidence baseline mechanism (already established by Phase 4K.2), NOT this checkpoint's freshness/terminal-window/adherence-confidence machinery, because no completed-history evidence yet exists to evaluate; it remains subject to the same safety and feasibility validation defined here. The production contract for representing this distinction (e.g. an InitialActivation state) is deferred to a future implementation phase. (17) PROFILE POLICY -- identical freshness, terminal-window, partial/missed/NotToday treatment, adherence-confidence rule, safety handling, and state-transition table for both CONSISTENCY_NEEDED and CORE_ENTRY_READY; no profile-specific decision threshold is approved -- profile differences remain confined to workout content selection. (18) NON-CLAIMS recorded verbatim: checkpoint state is a product-planning decision, not a medical diagnosis; adherence does not directly measure fitness; completed volume does not prove injury safety; stale evidence cannot prove detraining; MaintenanceOnly does not mean the athlete regressed; GrowthEligible does not guarantee improved performance; no universal adherence percentage is claimed (none was found, none was invented); HRV and wearable data are not required. Zero new adherence percentage, zero new evidence-age duration beyond the existing 4-week activation-window default, zero medical-scoring system, and zero production code were introduced.
