risks.closureNote: Phase 4K.4 approved: (1) REPOSITORY DEPENDENCY FINDING -- direct source inspection proves the existing, unmodified Preparation Runway numeric pipeline (PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer/CalendarComposer/PaceMaterializer) REQUIRES a Core Week-1 numeric and pace target as a required, validated, non-null input, and Runway's own weekly-volume/long-run values are computed as a direct linear interpolation TOWARD that target -- this is a real, existing architectural coupling (confirmed by PHASE4I_6A's own documented rationale: computing Core first avoids a circular dependency where Runway would need a boundary to ramp toward before that boundary exists). This finding, not invention, drives every timing decision below. (2) ATOMIC RUNWAY+CORE RESOLUTION -- because Runway's numeric materializer cannot execute without a resolved Core Week-1 target, RunwayNumericContextResolution and CoreNumericContextResolution (for Core's Week-1 target specifically) are resolved ATOMICALLY, at the SAME checkpoint: the checkpoint that activates the first four-week rolling window (Phase 4K.1) containing any Runway week. In exact week-boundary terms: if the last GE week is global week N and the first Runway week is N+1, atomic Runway+Core-target resolution occurs at the checkpoint that activates the window whose EndWeek >= N+1 and StartWeek <= N+1 -- no separate synthetic checkpoint is inserted merely because a segment boundary falls inside a four-week window (reaffirming Phase 4K.1's mixed-window rule). (3) CORE'S FULL SCHEDULE VS ACTIVATED CORE WEEKS -- the existing, unmodified TenKPreparationRunwayCoreGenerator/DynamicCoreCalendarMaterializationOrchestrator pipeline computes ALL of Core's numeric weeks (not just Week 1) as an unavoidable byproduct of its own unchanged internal structure; this phase approves that ONLY the Core weeks falling within the CURRENTLY activating rolling window (if any, per Phase 4K.1's GE->Runway extension rule applied identically to Runway->Core) are ACTIVATED and exposed as executable prescriptions -- Core weeks beyond that window remain NumericPending (Phase 4K.1) and are explicitly NOT treated as authoritative; they are recomputed FRESH, via the same unchanged Core pipeline, at whichever future checkpoint eventually activates the window containing them, using THEN-current evidence and a fresh RuntimeConditionResolutionService call. (4) CORE WEEK-1 TARGET LOCKING -- because Core's Week-1 target is mathematically baked into every already-activated Runway week's interpolated value (see (1)), that specific target is LOCKED the moment it is used to activate any Runway numeric week, and must NOT be silently replaced for those already-activated weeks -- this is the REQUIRED invariant from this phase's own primary decision, satisfied here by combining 'atomic Runway+Core context locking at Runway entry' (for the Week-1 target, per (2)) WITH 'versioned future-only Core refresh with explicit compatibility validation' (for Core weeks 2+ not yet activated, per (3)) -- both principles apply simultaneously because they govern disjoint week sets, not because either was selected exclusively. A later, fresh Core refresh that would imply a DIFFERENT Week-1-equivalent target than the one already locked into activated Runway weeks is a segment-transition incompatibility, resolved by the EXISTING GE->Runway/Runway->Core validators and Phase 4I.6B's existing 'entry consolidation' policy -- not a new reconciliation formula. (5) JIT EVIDENCE SNAPSHOT -- this phase does NOT change either segment's existing, unmodified evidence source: Runway's starting evidence remains GE exit state (Phase 4I.6A, LongHorizonGeExitState), and Core's Week-1 target remains derived from the ORIGINAL, unmodified onboarding evidence (RecentWeeklyVolumeKm/RecentLongestRunKm/RecentRunsPerWeek via the plan's own PreviewRequest/ResolverInputSnapshot) -- exactly as the existing 15-20 week path already does; this phase governs ONLY the TIMING of when that existing, unmodified mechanism is invoked within a rolling multi-checkpoint plan (at the Runway-entry checkpoint, not once at initial full-plan generation), never a change to WHICH evidence feeds it. A conceptual JIT evidence snapshot for this checkpoint includes: current GE exit/validated evidence, current onboarding evidence (unchanged), current availability/preferred days/long-run-day, the immutable race date, current target-finish-time source and explicit value if supplied, current recent-race evidence if still fresh (existing PaceSourceResolver 30/60/90/180-day ladder, unchanged), the latest GE checkpoint decision, and safety-clear state; structurally planned future values never enter this snapshot (Phase 4K.3, reaffirmed). (6) EVIDENCE PRECEDENCE -- weekly-volume precedence for Runway's OWN entry evidence: (a) current validated sustainable weekly load from the last completed GE checkpoint (Phase 4K.2/4K.3, an explicit, DISCLOSED FUTURE CHANGE from today's code, which currently uses GE's own planned final-week progression value via LongHorizonGeExitState.From -- implementing this evidence-source swap for the rolling runtime is deferred, not performed by this phase); (b) prior still-valid validated load if the most recent checkpoint's evidence is itself stale; (c) otherwise blocked (JIT_VALIDATED_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE) -- planned GE exit never outranks actual validated evidence, and no averaging of incompatible sources is permitted. Long-run precedence mirrors this identically for ValidatedSustainableLongRunKm. Core's Week-1 target evidence precedence is NOT redefined by this phase (see (5)) -- it remains the existing onboarding-evidence-only mechanism, unchanged. (7) GE EXIT VERSUS ACTUAL EVIDENCE -- Runway entry is anchored to CURRENT VALIDATED ACTUAL evidence (Phase 4K.2's ValidatedSustainableWeeklyVolumeKm/ValidatedSustainableLongRunKm from the last completed GE checkpoint), not the last planned GE peak; planned GE exit may be retained as provenance/consistency-check context but must never override lower actual capacity nor force Runway upward. A material mismatch between planned and actual evidence is NOT silently ignored, but also requires NO new convergence percentage and NO new blocking rule: Runway's existing, unmodified interpolation formula already accepts any starting-evidence magnitude, and the existing Phase 4I.6B 'build toward' (actual below Core target) or 'entry consolidation' (actual at/above Core target) policies already fully govern both directions -- only an existing, independent feasibility failure (four-session infeasibility) blocks activation, never the magnitude mismatch itself. This phase's TODAY-code caveat: LongHorizonGeExitState.From's existing planned-progression-only computation remains valid ONLY for the non-rolling/full-upfront execution path (Phase 4I.6B.1's diagnostic scans, legacy/preview contexts); it is not redefined here. (8) RUNWAY EXIT VERSUS CORE ENTRY AUTHORITY -- Core's Week-1 target is NOT derived from the same evidence used at Runway entry (confirmed independent, intentional, per (5)/(1)'s circular-dependency rationale); Runway IS designed to converge/consolidate toward that target (existing interpolation formula, Phase 4I.6B); Core's Week-1 target context is frozen for already-activated Runway weeks (per (4)); it MAY be recalculated for NOT-YET-activated Core weeks (per (3)); such recalculation NEVER invalidates already-activated Runway prescriptions (per the REQUIRED invariant this phase enforces). (9) MIXED-SEGMENT WINDOW POLICY -- both the existing GE->Runway mixed window (Phase 4K.1, reaffirmed unchanged) and the newly-addressed Runway->Core mixed window (1-3 remaining Runway weeks + 1-3 following Core weeks in one rolling window) follow IDENTICAL principles: GE weeks use the Phase 4K.3 checkpoint Growth/Maintenance decision; Runway weeks use the approved JIT Runway context; Core weeks (when present in the same window) use the atomically co-resolved Core Week-1-adjacent target from (2); each week retains correct segment provenance and unchanged global week numbering; no synthetic recovery week is ever inserted; Runway/Core weeks are never treated as GE maintenance weeks. ATOMICITY (Option A approved): the entire four-week mixed window succeeds or none of it activates -- this is not merely preferred for schedule continuity, it is the ONLY option mechanically supportable by the existing, unmodified pipeline, since Core's Week-1 target is a hard, synchronous prerequisite of Runway's own numeric materialization (per (1)) -- partial activation (e.g. Runway succeeding while Core is blocked) is not something the current architecture can produce without deep pipeline changes explicitly out of scope for this phase. (10) RACE DATE AND TIME BUDGET -- the race date remains structurally authoritative and immutable (Phase 4K.1, reaffirmed); remaining weeks at JIT activation are calculated via simple subtraction against the immutable race date and the current calendar date, reusing the existing RaceHorizonPolicy/PreparationRunwayCalendarAuthorityAdapter unchanged; segment durations remain structurally fixed; a delayed checkpoint does NOT shorten Runway/Core or shift the race date -- if a delay leaves genuinely insufficient calendar time for the still-fixed remaining structural weeks, this is resolved via the EXISTING, unmodified TimeAdequacyResolver/goal-feasibility taxonomy (already part of RuntimeConditionResolutionService), never a new compressed-Long-Horizon formula. (11) TARGET-TIME AND PACE-SOURCE EVIDENCE -- reuses RuntimeConditionResolutionService, the existing target-time-source policy, and the existing recent-race freshness ladder verbatim and unmodified; weekly-volume freshness (4-week activation window, Phase 4K.3) is never reinterpreted as race-pace freshness (30/60/90/180-day ladder) or vice versa. Because RuntimeConditionResolutionService's own inputs (race date, target finish time, AsOfDate=plan start) are fixed and available from t=0 (confirmed by direct inspection -- nothing in ResolverInputSnapshot depends on GE or Runway numeric output), the pace/target context is RE-RESOLVED (the same unchanged service called again with a current AsOfDate) at the atomic Runway+Core-target checkpoint from (2), rather than reused frozen from initial plan creation; it is re-resolved AGAIN only if a later, versioned Core refresh (per (3)) occurs for not-yet-activated Core weeks, using the same unchanged service with then-current evidence. (12) AVAILABILITY AND CALENDAR EVIDENCE -- current PreferredDays/days-per-week/long-run-day are reconfirmed at JIT resolution using the identical Phase 4K.3 freshness policy (presumptively unchanged absent an explicit conflicting signal); four-session feasibility (existing, unmodified FourDaySessionDistanceAllocationPolicy) remains required for both Runway and Core numeric generation, exactly as today; completed history dates never move; only unstarted future weeks may receive revised dates; exact persistence/rescheduling mechanics are explicitly deferred, out of scope for this policy phase. (13) MISSING OR STALE JIT CONTEXT -- deterministic NumericActivationBlocked with exactly one typed reason (14) for every listed failure mode; explicitly FORBIDDEN fallbacks, reaffirmed verbatim: planned GE peak, stale original baseline, fabricated zero, generic product-average weekly volume, or GE maintenance rules applied to Runway/Core. (14) REASON TAXONOMY -- ten JIT-specific typed reasons approved, additive to and non-duplicative of Phase 4K.3's nine checkpoint reasons: RUNWAY_JIT_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE, CORE_JIT_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE, JIT_VALIDATED_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE, JIT_VALIDATED_LONG_RUN_UNAVAILABLE, JIT_PACE_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED, JIT_GOAL_FEASIBILITY_UNRESOLVED, JIT_AVAILABILITY_INFEASIBLE, JIT_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED, JIT_ACTIVATION_BOUNDARY_MISSED, JIT_SEGMENT_TRANSITION_INFEASIBLE; SAFETY_REASSESSMENT_REQUIRED (Phase 4K.3) is reused directly, not duplicated, and retains the highest evaluation priority here too; internal exception wording is never exposed as product copy; the existing, unrelated 53+ horizon rejection is unchanged and unaffected. (15) JIT RESULT MODEL -- conceptual JitContextApproved/JitContextBlocked outcomes identifying: activation boundary, segments covered, evidence snapshot provenance, weekly-volume authority, long-run authority, pace-source authority, target-time authority, goal-feasibility authority, a context version/decision identity, whether Runway and Core were resolved atomically, and validators required before activation; JitContextBlocked always carries exactly one authoritative reason from (14); production types are deferred to Phase 4K.5. (16) IMMUTABILITY AND VERSIONING PRINCIPLE -- completed weeks never change (existing); already-activated numeric weeks, INCLUDING the Core Week-1 target locked into their interpolation math (per (4)), never silently change; future pending weeks may receive a new JIT context; a JIT context used to activate weeks retains provenance; future-only recalculation produces a NEW decision identity/version rather than mutating the prior one in place; the structural roadmap remains entirely unchanged; no database table is designed by this phase. (17) PROFILE POLICY -- identical JIT timing, evidence precedence, blocked conditions, and context immutability for both CONSISTENCY_NEEDED and CORE_ENTRY_READY -- the reviewed Runway/Core generator code contains no profile-specific branching in its JIT evidence path; profile differences remain confined to workout content selection, matching every prior phase's finding. (18) NON-CLAIMS recorded verbatim: JIT resolution does not measure laboratory fitness; actual completed load does not guarantee race readiness; a current Core target is a planning input, not a physiological certainty; product-average target time is not an individualized performance prediction; JIT recalculation does not guarantee injury prevention; planned GE or Runway progression is not proof of adaptation; no medical or wearable requirement is introduced. Zero new convergence percentage, zero new evidence-freshness duration beyond the existing Phase 4K.3 default, zero Runway/Core/GE algorithm change, and zero production code were introduced -- every timing decision in this closure note is a direct, disclosed consequence of tracing the real, existing, unmodified pipeline's own hard dependencies, not invention. Final classification: LONG_HORIZON_RUNWAY_AND_CORE_JUST_IN_TIME_NUMERIC_CONTEXT_POLICY_APPROVED. See PHASE4K_4_RUNWAY_AND_CORE_JUST_IN_TIME_NUMERIC_CONTEXT_POLICY_RESOLUTION.md for the full record.

risks.statement: The dark, unwired Preparation Runway contract layer (PreparationRunwayContracts.cs) retains an AEROBIC_STRENGTH block type whose semantics were never formally resolved. Two candidate interpretations exist: (A) gym-based resistance/plyometric strength training, and (B) running-based controlled aerobic-power/economy stimulus (hills, strides, controlled fartlek, short aerobic intervals). This phase formally resolves the semantic question in favor of (B) -- interpretation (A) is rejected because the repository contains zero gym/resistance/plyometric content anywhere (an exhaustive grep of all 18 workout-definition documents in plan-catalog/catalog/workouts/ for hill/stride/plyometric/resistance/gym/strength/core/economy/power found zero matches), and approving a week-consuming runway block purely by citing general strength-training literature, with no catalog-executable content, would be exactly the kind of unsupported inference this phase is required to reject. However, even under the accepted interpretation (B), no catalog-executable workout exists today: the only running-based intensity-variation content anywhere in the catalog is FARTLEK's SURGE_AND_FLOAT pattern (family=QUALITY), which is restricted to eligiblePhases=[BUILD] only by the closed workout-definition schema enum -- there is no schema provision for a runway-eligible phase value, and no hill-repeat, stride, or short-aerobic-interval workout definition exists at all. AEROBIC_STRENGTH is therefore catalog-UNSUPPORTED under either semantic interpretation, independent of the semantic question itself. A second, independent finding compounds this: the coefficient-family simulation performed in this phase (Phase4G6A2CoefficientSimulationTests.cs, local/test-only) proved the CORE_ENTRY_READY candidate profile's target behavior matrix (AerobicStrengthSecondWeekThreshold = RunwayWeeks >= 6) is not mechanically reproducible by the described constrained-proportional/floor/largest-remainder allocator mechanism under any of the three tested coefficient pairs, nor under a deliberately extreme 0.85/0.15 weighting -- the block's second-week exposure emerges one horizon earlier (RunwayWeeks=5) under pure proportional weighting, regardless of coefficient choice. This is a structural finding (the target shape requires an explicit threshold-gated priority rule, not proportional-weight tuning), independent of and additional to the catalog-capacity blocker.

Separately, PreSpecificTransition's Phase 4G.6A.2 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED classification is upgraded to SUPPORTED: it is content-supported via the existing EASY_STANDARD/LONG_RUN_STANDARD workouts, functionally distinguished from GeneralEndurance and from Core's own FOUNDATION_EASY_BASE by fixed non-expandable position, a volume-settle (not volume-build) trajectory, and strict sequential non-overlap with Core's own calendar weeks -- directly precedented by the existing TAPER_SHARPEN stage, which already reuses EASY_STANDARD at the plan's opposite (pre-race) boundary without being considered a duplicate of FOUNDATION_EASY_BASE. The workout-definition schema's eligiblePhases enum was extended with PREPARATION_RUNWAY (plan-catalog/schemas/workout-definition.schema.json), and the corresponding production C# PhaseKey enum (plan-catalog/src/PlanCatalog.Contracts/Enums/PhaseKey.cs) was extended identically, since the real production loader deserializes this field strictly (JsonStringEnumConverter, no lenient fallback) -- all 18 pre-existing plus 2 new workout definitions re-verified schema-valid; existing FOUNDATION/BUILD/RACE_SPECIFIC/TAPER values re-verified still accepted; an unknown phase value re-verified still rejected. A new, separate, dark, deliberately-unregistered catalog document type (PREPARATION_RUNWAY_BLOCK_PROGRESSION; plan-catalog/schemas/preparation-runway-block-progression.schema.json; plan-catalog/catalog/preparation-runway-progressions/ten-k-aerobic-strength-progression.v1.json) records the canonical two-step progression (Step1=INTRO, Step2=PROGRESSED, Step1 precedes Step2, no third step, no RunwayWeeks inspection anywhere in its content) -- confirmed by direct source inspection that FileSystemCatalogSourceRepository only iterates 10 fixed subfolders and does not read this new folder, so the document is fully inert to the real loader. The two new workouts are confirmed, by direct construction of the REAL published bundle for TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE v10, absent from that bundle (unreferenced by ten-k-workout-progression.v5.json), and Core Week 1 (FOUNDATION_EASY_BASE) is confirmed to still candidate only EASY_STANDARD -- no duplication, no live reachability. risks.closureCriteriaSatisfied: All eight conditions from this TD's own closure standard are met: semantic contract remains resolved (unchanged, not reopened); a valid runway-eligible workout definition exists (two, in fact); one-week content is executable (INTRO, schema-valid); two-week progression is executable (INTRO then PROGRESSED, schema-valid, ordered); schema represents Preparation Runway eligibility (PREPARATION_RUNWAY, both JSON schema and C# enum); progression mapping validates (dedicated schema + tests); no unsupported repetition is required (no duplicate component types, validated by the existing WorkoutDefinitionValidator rule); no adjacent-phase duplication remains (disjoint eligiblePhases from GeneralEndurance/Transition/Core Week 1, proven by direct catalog-content tests, not assumption). risks.selectedMaterializationStrategy: Option A: generate the complete approved Runway prescription once at JIT entry, bind it to one immutable context/Core-target lock, and expose only exact selected-window references in each rolling activation.
risks.fullBlockAuthority: The existing complete 3-8-week materializer remains the only numeric authority. No slice independently runs interpolation and no second formula exists.
risks.boundedExposure: A rolling window projects only its requested 1-4 local Runway weeks from the immutable full prescription. Unselected computed weeks remain internal, non-executable and absent from roadmap numeric fields/public DTOs/persistence.
risks.interpolationCoordinates: Full duration, original start, locked target, full local week number, progress numerator=index, denominator=fullDuration-2, and selected slice offsets remain fixed from the full prescription. Slice-local progress never resets.
risks.localGlobalWeekMapping: Runway local week 1..N remains unchanged and maps to global week GeneralEnduranceWeeks+localWeek. Exposure never renumbers a slice as a new local block.
risks.preSpecificTransitionBehavior: Exactly one PreSpecificTransition exists at full local Runway week N. Earlier/middle slices never synthesize it; the final slice exposes that existing terminal week unchanged.
risks.targetLockScope: One immutable Core Week-1 target and one Runway prescription version cover the complete Runway global-week range, not separate locks per slice.
risks.futureEvidenceRefresh: No target or prescription refresh is permitted mid-Runway. New evidence may inform a later non-overlapping Core-only context after Runway ends; it cannot rewrite computed or activated Runway weeks.
risks.mixedWindowImplications: GE+Runway combines 4K.7 GE output with an exact locked Runway slice atomically; Runway-only exposes a slice; Runway+Core combines final locked Runway weeks with selected Core output atomically; Core-only is otherwise independent.
risks.internalComputationSafeguards: ComputedInternalPending is conceptual internal state, not a new public lifecycle enum. It creates no TrainingDay, checkpoint evidence, achieved-load authority, DTO value or persisted future prescription.
risks.implementationImpact: Phase 4K.8B must implement the narrow immutable full-prescription/bounded-exposure contract and validators. Phase 4K.8 runtime remains unimplemented until then.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE v10 Long-Horizon rolling Runway specifically.
risks.closureNote: Unchanged full-block diagnostics cover both profiles and durations 3-8; slice projections for first, middle and final 1-4-week ranges are byte-equivalent references to the authoritative full output. Independent slice restart is rejected because it changes coordinates and may fail or produce different values.
risks.addendum: UPDATE (Phase 4K.8B, append-only): the full-prescription/week-reference/bounded-slice/exact-equivalence contracts this decision required are now implemented as dark production contracts (ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescription, PreparationRunwayPrescriptionWeekReference, BoundedPreparationRunwayPrescriptionSlice, PreparationRunwayBoundedSliceFactory/EquivalenceValidator), reusing the unchanged PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer output directly (never recalculated). risks.title: Preparation Runway Direction Guard and Bounded Prescription Production Contracts Implemented -- Dark, Unwired, Zero Formula Change, Phase 4K.8 JIT Runtime Still Absent
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4K.8B -- Preparation Runway Direction Guard and Bounded Prescription Contract Implementation (2026-08-03). Implements contracts, validators and a narrow factory only -- no Runway/Core JIT orchestration, no mixed-segment window activation, no downward interpolation enabled, no persistence/API/preview/DI/Flutter change.
risks.source: Direct implementation of TD-LONG-HORIZON-RUNWAY-DOWNWARD-CONSOLIDATION-AUTHORITY-001/TD-LONG-HORIZON-BOUNDED-RUNWAY-MATERIALIZATION-001's approved authorities as real C# types in backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/PreparationRunway/ (9 files), reusing the unchanged PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer/PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializerTests fixtures directly rather than any hand-built shortcut. 70 new backend tests in RunningApp.IntegrationTests/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/PreparationRunway/.
risks.directionRelationContract: PreparationRunwayDirectionRelation (BelowTarget/EqualTarget/AboveTarget) plus one deterministic PreparationRunwayDirectionComparer using the existing 0.5km rounding granularity -- no new tolerance introduced, no ad hoc comparison scattered across validators.
risks.directionGuard: PreparationRunwayDirectionGuard.Evaluate returns a PreparationRunwayDirectionPolicy: weekly/long-run BelowTarget and EqualTarget are conditionally supported (existing downstream validators still govern actual feasibility); AboveTarget is unsupported for both, independently evaluated (weekly support never masks an independent long-run conflict) -- mapped to the existing JIT_SEGMENT_TRANSITION_INFEASIBLE reason via the shared LongHorizonReasonCode abstraction, never a new public reason.
risks.fullPrescriptionContract: ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescription<TKey> wraps the unchanged PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer output with a deterministic PrescriptionId/PrescriptionVersion (SHA-256, reusing the existing LongHorizonRollingCheckpointRuntime.StableGuid convention -- no random GUID, no wall clock), duration 3-8 weeks, contiguous unique local/global week coordinates (global = start + local - 1), a required target-lock whose range must exactly equal the prescription's own range, and ComputedInternalPending=true / Immutable=true always.
risks.weekReferenceContract: PreparationRunwayPrescriptionWeekReference<TKey>.ProductionWeek IS the original PreparationRunwayPrescribedWeek<TKey> instance -- WeeklyVolumeKm/LongRunKm/Stage are read from it, never recomputed or duplicated.
risks.targetLockScope: PreparationRunwayTargetLockScope/Validator plus PreparationRunwayTargetRefreshGuard.ValidateRefreshOutsideRunwayRange reject any per-slice lock and any new context whose range overlaps an already-locked full Runway range (mid-Runway refresh forbidden); a strictly later ContextVersion is required for any accepted future context, reusing the same overlap-check shape as LongHorizonCoreTargetLockValidator.ValidateRefresh rather than inventing a split-Runway policy.
risks.boundedSliceContract: BoundedPreparationRunwayPrescriptionSlice<TKey> (1-4 contiguous local weeks) is produced only by PreparationRunwayBoundedSliceFactory.CreateSlice, which never invokes the numeric materializer (its signature structurally cannot -- it takes an already-built ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescription, not a materialization request), never mutates the source prescription, and returns the identical (record-equal) week-reference instances filtered from the full prescription.
risks.exactEquivalenceValidator: PreparationRunwayBoundedSliceEquivalenceValidator runs inside the factory itself (not only in tests), proving every slice week is value-equal to its corresponding full-prescription week reference across prescription/version identity, local/global week, stage, weekly volume, long run, production-week reference, and full-output index -- no field recomputed or replaced.
risks.terminalStageInvariant: PreparationRunwayTerminalStageValidator enforces PreSpecificTransition occurs exactly once, on local week = FullRunwayDurationWeeks; an earlier or missing occurrence throws PreparationRunwayTerminalStageViolationException. First/middle slices never synthesize the terminal stage; the final slice exposes the pre-existing terminal week reference unchanged.
risks.internalPendingSafeguards: ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescription<TKey> and BoundedPreparationRunwayPrescriptionSlice<TKey> carry no LongHorizonNumericLifecycleState field at all -- they structurally cannot represent NumericActivated. No TrainingDay, checkpoint-evidence, public DTO, or persistence type is referenced anywhere in the new PreparationRunway namespace (confirmed by reflection-based tests).
risks.deterministicIdentity: PreparationRunwayDeterministicIdentity.StableGuid reuses the exact SHA-256 convention already used by LongHorizonRollingCheckpointRuntime/LongHorizonRollingInitialActivationRuntime. Identical full materializer output + target lock always yields the same PrescriptionId/PrescriptionVersion/SliceId; changed target lock, evidence, duration, or slice range always yields a different one -- proven by 6 dedicated determinism tests.
risks.validatorOrder: PreparationRunwayFullPrescriptionFactory<TKey>.Create executes: (1) normalized direction comparison, (2) direction-policy support (throws PreparationRunwayDirectionUnsupportedException if AboveTarget for either weekly or long run), (3) target-lock validation, then delegates (4)-(7) full-duration/week-count, local/global coordinates, PreSpecificTransition, and immutability/reference validation to ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescriptionValidator; slice creation separately runs (8)-(9) range and exact-equivalence validation inside PreparationRunwayBoundedSliceFactory.
risks.integrationStatus: Zero existing public DTO, preview response, orchestrator, DI registration, or database entity/migration touched -- confirmed by a clean build of RunningApp.Application/RunningApp.Api with no file outside the new PreparationRunway subfolder modified.
risks.phase4K8RuntimeStatus: Still entirely absent -- no Runway/Core JIT orchestration, no Core generation invocation, no validated-load mapping, no pace resolution, no calendar generation, and no mixed-segment window activation exist anywhere in this namespace. PreparationRunwayBoundedExposureSelection (Part 16) is defined but never activated.

risks.title: Runway and Core JIT Numeric Runtime and Mixed-Segment Window Activation Implemented -- Dark, Unwired, Atomic GE+Runway/Runway-Only/Runway+Core/Core-Only Activation, No Numeric Formula Change
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4K.8 -- Runway and Core JIT Numeric Runtime and Mixed-Segment Window Activation (2026-08-03). Implements the dark orchestration runtime that resolves and atomically activates the next rolling window when it involves Preparation Runway and/or Core -- consumes, never redesigns, the Phase 4K.5/4K.8B typed contracts.
risks.source: backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/LongHorizonRollingJitActivationRuntime.cs and LongHorizonRollingJitActivationContracts.cs. 41 new backend tests in RunningApp.IntegrationTests/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/LongHorizonRollingJitActivationRuntimeTests.cs, built through real, unchanged PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer calls via the existing PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializerTests fixture helpers.
risks.runtimeEntryPoint: ILongHorizonRollingJitActivationRuntime.ResolveAndActivateNextWindowAsync, implemented by LongHorizonRollingJitActivationRuntime -- internal, parameterless-constructible, no public DI registration.
risks.eligibility: Race / exact 10K / Intermediate / four days per week / 21-52 structural horizon / valid readiness profile matching the structural roadmap -- enforced by ValidateInput; does not alter the 8-14 Core-only, 15-20 Runway+Core, 53+ rejection, Habit, or other-distance/level/frequency flows, none of which this runtime touches.
risks.windowSelection: WindowStart = first global week whose lifecycle state is NumericPending; WindowEnd = the last contiguous NumericPending week up to min(WindowStart+3, TotalWeeks). A pure GE-only window (both boundary weeks in GeneralEndurance) is explicitly out of this runtime's scope (Phase 4K.7's own) and blocks with JIT_SEGMENT_TRANSITION_INFEASIBLE rather than being silently handled.
risks.jitEvidenceAuthority: Weekly/long-run authority is the caller-supplied ValidatedSustainableLoad (Phase 4K.5A rolling authority) -- onboarding evidence and planned GE exit are never read as rolling authority anywhere in this runtime. Pace/goal-feasibility context is the caller's own already-resolved RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAllResults output (never recomputed internally, exactly mirroring how the real, unmodified TenKPreparationRunwayCoreGenerationRequest/DynamicCoreCalendarMaterializationContext already take ConditionResults as a pre-resolved input).
risks.coreInputMapping: LongHorizonJitCoreInputAdapter.Map implements the exact Phase 4K.5A mapping (ValidatedSustainableLoad.WeeklyVolumeKm -> RecentWeeklyVolumeKm, LongRunKm -> RecentLongestRunKm, exact completed frequency -> RecentRunsPerWeek or null, never rounded/inferred); it throws if the supplied load is not Valid, and the returned mapping's evidence-authority records can never carry OriginalOnboardingEvidence (Phase 4K.5's own guard already prevents that at construction).
risks.coreTargetGeneration: This runtime does not itself invoke TenKPreparationRunwayCoreGenerator or the five-layer DynamicCoreCalendarMaterializationOrchestrator -- exactly like that generator's own request type, it accepts the caller's already-produced PreparationRunwayCoreWeekOneNumericTarget (from the real, unchanged TenKPreparationRunwayCoreGenerator + PreparationRunwayCoreWeekOneTargetAdapter chain) and AvailableCoreWeeks (the caller's own real, unchanged Core generation output) as inputs, then locks/bounds/selects from them -- disclosed explicitly, not hidden, and consistent with every prior phase's own 'the existing Core generator remains authoritative, never reimplemented' boundary.
risks.directionGuard: Reuses Phase 4K.8B's PreparationRunwayDirectionGuard verbatim inside PreparationRunwayFullPrescriptionFactory.Create (called from ResolveOrCreateRunwayPrescription) -- weekly/long-run BelowTarget/EqualTarget continue, AboveTarget throws PreparationRunwayDirectionUnsupportedException, caught by this runtime's own outer try/catch and mapped to JIT_SEGMENT_TRANSITION_INFEASIBLE. No downward interpolation, target lift, or evidence lowering exists anywhere in this runtime.
risks.targetLockCreationAndReuse: First Runway entry creates exactly one LongHorizonLockedCoreWeekOneTarget whose LockedForActivatedRunwayWeekRange exactly equals the structural Runway segment's full range; continuation windows reuse the caller-supplied ExistingLockedCoreTarget/ExistingRunwayPrescription unchanged (range-compatibility re-verified, never regenerated) via ResolveOrCreateRunwayPrescription's own reuse branch.
risks.fullRunwayMaterialization: The unchanged, real PreparationRunwayNumericMaterializer.Materialize is called exactly once, at first Runway entry, via TenKPreparationRunwayNumericPolicyFactory.Build() and the caller-supplied RunwayStructuralWeeks/RunwayStartingLoadEvidence; its successful result is passed to PreparationRunwayFullPrescriptionFactory.Create (Phase 4K.8B, unmodified) to produce one ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescription. Later windows never call the materializer again -- proven by ResolveOrCreateRunwayPrescription's reuse branch and by determinism tests.
risks.boundedRunwayExposure: SliceForWindow maps the selected global-week range to the prescription's own local-week coordinates and calls PreparationRunwayBoundedSliceFactory.CreateSlice (Phase 4K.8B, unmodified) -- exact week references, no recalculation, no local renumbering; MapRunwayWeeks converts only the selected slice's references into real NumericActivated ActivatedNumericWeek instances.
risks.geRunwayBehavior: ActivateGeRunwayMixedWindow requires the caller's own already-materialized GeActivatedWeeks (Phase 4K.6/4K.7's real GE materializers, never recomputed by this runtime) for the GE portion and the bounded Runway slice for the Runway portion, concatenated into one atomic window; a failure in either portion (missing GE weeks, or an unsupported Runway direction) propagates through the shared try/catch, producing zero activated weeks for the whole window.
risks.runwayOnlyBehavior: ActivateRunwayOnlyWindow reuses an existing compatible prescription/lock when present (continuation) or creates them at first entry; an incompatible existing prescription (range mismatch) throws PreparationRunwayTargetLockScopeViolationException, caught and mapped to a blocked result.
risks.runwayCoreBehavior: ActivateRunwayCoreMixedWindow requires an already-existing, immutable full Runway prescription (Runway's own materializer always completes before its final window is reached) plus caller-supplied AvailableCoreWeeks for the Core portion; both portions are combined into one atomic window with correct per-segment provenance; future Core weeks beyond the selected range remain NumericPending.
risks.coreOnlyBehavior: ActivateCoreOnlyWindow requires the window to begin strictly after the Runway segment's own EndGlobalWeek (else PreparationRunwayMidRunwayRefreshViolationException) and a complete contiguous set of caller-supplied AvailableCoreWeeks for the requested range; already-activated/completed Core weeks are never touched (only the LifecycleStates dictionary's NumericPending entries within the selected range change).
risks.futureCoreRefresh: Not implemented as an explicit refresh operation in this phase (out of scope, consistent with 'Do not implement full 21-52 lifecycle simulation') -- the underlying versioning primitives (LongHorizonContextVersion.Next, PreparationRunwayTargetRefreshGuard from Phase 4K.8B) that a future refresh call would use are unchanged and available; this runtime's own Core-only path simply selects from whatever AvailableCoreWeeks the caller supplies for that invocation.
risks.calendarPaceBehavior: Calendar continuity reuses the existing, real, pure LongHorizonCalendarAssigner.WeekStartDate primitive (the same one Phase 4K.6/4K.7's GE runtimes already use) applied to Runway and Core weeks too, rather than wiring the heavier, DI-dependent PreparationRunwayCalendarComposer -- an explicitly disclosed simplification, not a fabrication, since WeekStartDate is real, unchanged, already-tested production code; pace/goal feasibility is read directly from the caller's own real RuntimeConditionResolutionService output (HasUnresolvedPaceOrGoal), never recomputed.
risks.atomicityAndLifecycle: Every segment-activation path is wrapped by one shared try/catch in ResolveAndActivateNextWindowAsync: any LongHorizonRollingContractException thrown anywhere (direction guard, target-lock validation, full-prescription validation, bounded-slice validation, numeric-week validation, window validation) produces a Blocked result with zero newly activated weeks and prior LifecycleStates entries fully preserved -- proven by dedicated atomicity tests.
risks.determinismAndVersioning: JIT decision ID, context version, and (via Phase 4K.5/4K.8B) target-lock/prescription/slice/window IDs are all SHA-256-derived from an explicit input seed (BuildIdentitySeed) reusing the exact StableGuid convention already used by LongHorizonRollingCheckpointRuntime/LongHorizonRollingInitialActivationRuntime -- no random GUID, no wall-clock read; identical inputs reproduce identical prescription/window identities, proven by dedicated determinism tests.
risks.boundedExecutionProof: Dedicated tests prove: the full Runway materializer runs exactly once across a multi-window activation chain; only the selected window's weeks transition to NumericActivated while the rest of the roadmap remains NumericPending; no more than one window activates per invocation; and the RollingActivation namespace references no controller/DbContext/public DTO type.
risks.persistencePublicStatus: Unchanged. Zero controller, DI registration, database entity/migration, or Flutter file touched -- confirmed by a clean build of RunningApp.Application/RunningApp.Api with no file outside the new runtime/contracts files modified.
risks.tests: 41 new focused tests, all passing on first run after two window-selection-premise corrections, covering authority/mapping, safety-first blocking, window selection (including GE-only out-of-scope), the direction guard (below/equal/above), full Runway materialization, GE+Runway/Runway-only/Runway+Core/Core-only activation chains (including a genuine multi-window chain proving a Runway+Core mixed window arises naturally from a non-multiple-of-four Runway remainder), continuation/reuse, atomicity, determinism, bounded-execution, and both readiness profiles.
risks.phase4K8DUpdate: APPEND-ONLY UPDATE (Phase 4K.8D, 2026-08-03): Phase 4K.8's window selection, numeric mapping, target locking, direction guard, bounded slicing, lifecycle mutation and atomicity remain unchanged. risks.phase4K8DUpdate: APPEND-ONLY UPDATE (Phase 4K.8D, 2026-08-03): the disclosed final-calendar gap is closed. risks.publicPreviewSemantics: A Long-Horizon public preview = the complete structural roadmap for all TotalWeeks (21-52) + the currently activated numeric window (at most 4 weeks, full session/date/volume detail) + explicit Pending representation for every future week, with no claim that future weeks are already finalized. Required wording bans ('complete schedule ready', 'all workouts finalized', 'confirmed future volume') are honored structurally: LongHorizonStructuralRoadmapWeekContract carries no numeric/session fields at all for Pending/Blocked rows -- there is no field to leak a false claim through, not just a convention not to populate one.
risks.structuralRoadmapContract: LongHorizonStructuralRoadmapWeekContract: GlobalWeek, public Phase (GeneralEndurance/PreparationRunway/Core), Stage, public LifecycleStatus, IsExecutable, StructuralStartDate/EndDate (pure StartDate + (GlobalWeek-1)*7 arithmetic, never a materializer read -- this is what keeps date boundaries safe to expose even for Pending weeks), NumericDetailsAvailable, PublicSummary message key. All TotalWeeks appear exactly once, globally contiguous, phase order GeneralEndurance->PreparationRunway->Core enforced by LongHorizonPublicPreviewContractValidator.
risks.executableWeekContract: LongHorizonExecutableWeekContract carries WeeklyVolumeKm/LongRunVolumeKm/WeekStartDate/WeekEndDate copied exactly from the real ActivatedNumericWeek (never recomputed), plus LongHorizonExecutableSessionContract per session with the exact real AssignedDate from the Phase 4K.8D calendar projection (Phase 4K.8C's own disclosed calendar-composition gap is resolved by 4K.8D, confirmed directly -- ActivatedNumericWeek.CalendarDates and each session's AssignedDate are populated by real, unmodified production authorities, not this phase's own computation).
risks.pendingWeekContract: A Pending roadmap row exposes only GlobalWeek/Phase/Stage/structural date range/status/summary message key -- no distance, no session, no workout key, no AssignedDate. LongHorizonStructuralRoadmapWeekContract has no property capable of carrying any of those, so leakage is structurally impossible, not merely avoided by convention (proven by LongHorizonPublicPreviewLeakageGuardTests.NoFutureWeeklyVolumeLeaksForPendingWeeks).
risks.blockedWeekContract: LongHorizonBlockedStateContract: Status=Blocked, one public ReasonCategory (MoreTrainingDataNeeded/CompleteCurrentWeek/UpdateAvailability/SafetyReviewRequired/PaceInformationNeeded/PlanTransitionUnavailable), RetryEligible (false only for SafetyReviewRequired), NextActionKey, LastEvaluatedDate. All nine LongHorizonCheckpointReasonCode and ten LongHorizonJitReasonCode values map deterministically to exactly one category (LongHorizonPublicPreviewMapper.MapReasonToCategory, exhaustively tested). A prior successfully activated window remains fully exposed (Available) even while a later window is Blocked -- the plan itself remains valid and previewable.
risks.publicLifecycleMapping: LongHorizonPublicLifecycleStatus {Available, Pending, Blocked, Completed, Missed} maps 1:1 from the five internal states the phase prompt specifies (NumericActivated/NumericPending/NumericActivationBlocked/Completed/Missed); StructurallyPlanned additionally collapses into Pending (both mean 'not yet executable', disclosed explicitly as a deliberate simplification with no distinct public meaning). Internal-only states (target-lock/context-refresh/prescription-created) never appear in the public enum at all.
risks.previewReadiness: ReadyForPublicPreview. Every real dark lifecycle snapshot (initial, mid-lifecycle, mixed-window, blocked, fully completed, both readiness profiles, horizons 21/25/29/40/52) maps to a contract that passes LongHorizonPublicPreviewContractValidator -- proven, not assumed.
risks.confirmationReadiness: NotReadyForConfirmation. Direct repository inspection (PlanServices.ConfirmPlanAsync, CatalogPlanConfirmationService.ConfirmAsync, the legacy GeneratePreviewResponse-deserialization path) confirms Answer B from Part 15: the current confirmation flow requires a complete, fully-numeric, fully-dated static schedule (throws CatalogPreviewNotPersistableException if GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload is null; the legacy path guards Weeks.Count==0 and derives plan start/end dates from the full Weeks array) and writes TrainingPlan/TrainingWeek/TrainingDay rows synchronously from that array in one call. A Long-Horizon preview with 17-48 Pending weeks cannot satisfy this without inventing values -- confirmation is not attempted, silently degraded, or worked around; it is left explicitly blocked.
risks.persistenceReadiness: Blocked/requires new persistence. TrainingWeek and TrainingDay carry no Pending/Blocked/Available lifecycle status field (TrainingDayStatus's seven values track completion/missed/rescheduled outcomes, not not-yet-generated state). PlanPreview stores only RequestPayloadJson/PreviewPayloadJson as opaque JSON. None of ValidatedSustainableLoad, checkpoint decisions, block/retry history, Core context versions, the Runway prescription identity, the target lock, or the session calendar projection have any persistence representation today -- all would require new schema, not a public-contract change.
risks.restartResumeReadiness: Blocked. No durable source of truth exists today from which the dark lifecycle's LongHorizonFullDarkLifecycleState (or any subset of it) could be reconstructed after a process restart -- there is nothing to query. A future phase should prefer persisting the minimal durable facts (structural roadmap parameters, last checkpoint evidence identity, locked target/prescription identity, activated-week numeric snapshots) and deterministically re-deriving lifecycle classification from them, rather than persisting full internal object graphs -- a direction noted for Phase 4L.2, not decided here.
risks.apiReadiness: Recommended strategy: (B) a dedicated Long-Horizon preview response discriminator/contract, not (A) extending GeneratePreviewResponse. GeneratePreviewResponse.PreviewWeekDto/PreviewDayDto have non-nullable Date/DistanceKm/DurationMin/Intensity and a non-nullable Days list on every existing week -- there is no nullable/optional seam anywhere in that DTO to carry a Pending week without either a breaking change or a dishonest placeholder value. No endpoint routing was changed by this phase.
risks.flutterReadiness: Not inspected code-level in this phase (explicitly out of scope -- 'do not modify Flutter'); by direct analogy to the backend finding, the existing generate-preview Dart DTOs mirror GeneratePreviewResponse's fully-populated-array assumption, so the same structural/pending/blocked rendering gaps documented in the phase document are expected to apply. Confirmed unchanged: zero Flutter files touched.
risks.leakageGuard: LongHorizonPublicPreviewLeakageGuardTests.PublicContractGraphExposesNoForbiddenInternalTypes walks the complete public contract type graph via reflection and asserts none of  ever appear as a property type anywhere in the graph -- structural, not convention-based, leakage prevention.
risks.privacyReview: The contract carries no raw TrainingDay evidence rows, no historical actual-performance detail beyond what is already publicly approved (a session's own real distance/date), no internal safety diagnostics, no internal confidence calculations, no internal catalog workout keys/versions, and no internal governance reason codes -- blocked reasons are always one of six public categories, never a raw LongHorizonReasonCode.

No future session arrays and no full internal Core/Runway output are ever included, by construction.

Consumes LongHorizonFullDarkLifecycleState (Phase 4K.9) plus plan-level context (StartDate/EstimatedEndDate/PreferredDays/LongRunDay/DaysPerWeek/GoalType/GoalDistance/ProvenanceSummary) supplied by the caller. Not exposed through any endpoint by this phase.

risks.liveWiringStatus: Zero live wiring exists or was added. No endpoint references LongHorizonPublicPreviewMapper (grepped directly against PlansController.cs); no DI registration exists (grepped against Program.cs); the mapper, all contract types, and the validator are internal, non-public C# types. risks.closureNote: The public preview contract for Long-Horizon plans is approved (dark): LongHorizonPublicPreviewMapper produces a complete structural roadmap plus the currently executable window plus explicit non-leaking Pending/Blocked representation, from real Phase 4K.9 dark lifecycle snapshots, validated by LongHorizonPublicPreviewContractValidator and proven leakage-free by dedicated reflection-based guard tests. risks.phase4L3Update: APPEND-ONLY UPDATE (Phase 4L.3, 2026-08-04): confirmation now reuses InitializeStructuralStateAsync inside one explicit transaction and links the durable rolling aggregate to a real user-owned TrainingPlan via PlanScheduleStrategy.RollingLongHorizon. risks.durableStateClassification: Plan/week/session identity, structural dates, lifecycle state, executable numeric values, and session AssignedDate/role/distance are persisted as authoritative durable state (Category A). The GE structural skeleton's workout ROLE labels are persisted as source facts and deterministically reconstructed (Category B) by re-invoking the exact unmodified LongHorizonStructuralMaterializer against the plan's own stored (TotalWeeks, ReadinessProfile, CandidateKey/Version) -- safe because that generation is evidence-independent, unlike Runway/Core numeric materialization. The immutable Runway prescription and selected Core weeks are persisted as bounded, versioned, immutable JSON snapshots (Category C) rather than regenerated, since their generation IS evidence-fed and byte-identical re-derivation is not guaranteed across future code/catalog/resolver/rounding changes. Raw internal diagnostic traces, full un-selected future Core output, and internal audit-event detail are not persisted (Category D).
risks.aggregateModel: LongHorizonRollingPlanState is deliberately NOT a TrainingPlans row: no GoalType.LongHorizon/GoalDistance.LongHorizon enum value exists yet (confirmed absent, Phase 4L.1), so there is no honest way to create a real TrainingPlan row without fabricating a meaning that doesn't exist. Its own Id is the internal ownership anchor for every child table. Carries TotalWeeks/ReadinessProfile/StartDate/RaceDate/GoalType/GoalDistance/Level/DaysPerWeek/PreferredDays/LongRunDay/CandidateKey/CandidateVersion/CatalogRootPath, CurrentLifecycleStatus/CurrentWindowStartWeek/EndWeek/LastActivatedGlobalWeek/LatestCheckpointDate/ActiveContextVersionSequence/ActiveContextVersionId, CurrentBlockedPublicReasonCategory/InternalReasonCode/BlockedAt/RetryEligible, PersistenceContractVersion, and a Postgres xmin-backed optimistic concurrency token.
risks.structuralWeekModel: LongHorizonRollingWeekState: exactly one row per (PlanStateId, GlobalWeek) enforced by a unique index. Carries SegmentType/Stage/StructuralStartDate/EndDate/LifecycleState plus nullable WeeklyVolumeKm/LongRunKm (populated only when Activated/Completed/Missed, enforced by the integrity validator, never a fabricated zero for Pending rows) and ActivationContextVersionSequence/ActivatedAtUtc/CompletedAtUtc/BlockedReasonCode/BlockedDecisionId.
risks.executableSessionOwnership: Deliberately NOT TrainingDay rows: TrainingDay.PlanId is a required FK to TrainingPlans, and Long-Horizon plans intentionally have no real TrainingPlan row -- reusing TrainingDay would require either fabricating a TrainingPlan row (forbidden) or a nullable PlanId (a breaking change to a table read by the real Home/Calendar/Details/completion endpoints, risking dark session leakage into live user-facing surfaces). LongHorizonRollingSessionState is a dedicated table, fully isolated from every live read path, with a unique (WeekStateId, SessionOrdinal) index.
risks.checkpointPersistence: LongHorizonCheckpointRecord is an immutable decision snapshot (AsOfDate, source window, evidence fingerprint, validated weekly/long-run volume, decision, authoritative reason), unique per (PlanStateId, AsOfDate, SourceWindowStartWeek) for idempotency. Raw TrainingDay-equivalent evidence is never duplicated into this table -- it remains the caller's own source facts, matching the phase's own 'do not persist unnecessary internal computation' guidance.
risks.runwayLockPrescriptionPersistence: Decision A (not B): LongHorizonRunwayState persists the immutable activated-authority prescription values (per-week global week/weekly volume/long run/stage) as a bounded, versioned jsonb snapshot, created exactly once per plan (enforced by a unique index on PlanStateId) and never regenerated on restart -- Decision B (rerun the materializer after restart) was rejected because equivalence across future code/catalog/resolver/rounding changes is not guaranteed and this phase does not attempt to prove it.
risks.coreContextPersistence: LongHorizonCoreContextRecord persists ContextVersionSequence/EffectiveFromGlobalWeek/EffectiveToGlobalWeek/AsOfDate plus bounded jsonb snapshots of the condition-result summary and selected Core weeks (same Decision-A rationale as Runway). A new context creation marks the prior Active context Superseded; activated Core weeks retain their original context ownership since only future Pending weeks are affected by a later refresh.
risks.blockRetryPersistence: LongHorizonBlockRetryRecord is an immutable audit trail (Block/RetryRequested/RetryRestored). SaveRetryRestorationAsync enforces, at the repository level: the plan must currently be NumericActivationBlocked (direct Blocked->Activated has no code path at all -- no repository method performs that transition); RetryCheckpointDate must be strictly later than the prior checkpoint date (same-date retry rejected); the evidence fingerprint must differ from the most recent Block record's fingerprint (unchanged-evidence retry rejected). Both rejections are proven against a real blocked plan in Postgres, not simulated.
risks.persistenceVersioning: PersistenceContractVersion=1, stored on the plan aggregate, checked during reconstruction; any value other than 1 throws LongHorizonRollingPersistenceCorruptionException (fail-closed, proven directly by mutating a real row to 999 and reconstructing).
risks.transactionBoundaries: Every Save* operation relies on EF Core's own implicit per-SaveChangesAsync transaction (the existing codebase never uses explicit BeginTransaction/CommitAsync either, confirmed absent by direct inspection) -- one SaveChangesAsync call covers the plan aggregate update, week-state updates, session inserts, and the activation-window/checkpoint/Runway/Core records together, so a mid-write failure rolls back the entire operation atomically.
risks.concurrency: A Postgres xmin-backed optimistic concurrency token on LongHorizonRollingPlanState. Every Save* method sets its EF change-tracker's original xmin value to the caller-supplied ExpectedConcurrencyVersion before SaveChangesAsync; a stale value throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException, mapped to a typed ConcurrencyConflict outcome (never silently swallowed or treated as success) -- proven directly: a winner writes first, a loser reusing the now-stale version is rejected.
risks.idempotency: Deterministic idempotency keys derived from (PlanStateId, week range, context version sequence, checkpoint/retry date) -- never a random request ID. InitializeStructuralStateAsync checks for an existing plan row before writing; SaveActivationSuccessAsync/SaveBlockAsync/SaveRetryRestorationAsync each check for an existing record with the same deterministic key/signature before writing and return IdempotentReplay without a duplicate write if found -- proven directly: replaying the identical block request produces exactly one durable block record, not two.
risks.reconstruction: LongHorizonRollingStateReconstructionService.ReconstructAsync assembles a real LongHorizonFullDarkLifecycleState (the exact type Phase 4K.9's runtimes consume -- no parallel shape invented) from durable rows plus the deterministically regenerated structural skeleton, running LongHorizonRollingPersistenceIntegrityValidator.ValidateWeekRows/ValidateReconstructedState before returning. No numeric or calendar value is ever regenerated -- proven directly: two independent reconstructions of the same persisted plan produce byte-identical activated-week volumes and session dates.
risks.restartContinuation: LongHorizonRollingRestartContinuationService.ContinueGeCheckpointAsync proves the full chain -- load restart snapshot from a brand-new AppDbContext/connection, map to the exact unmodified Phase 4K.7 LongHorizonRollingCheckpointRequest shape, invoke the real unmodified checkpoint runtime for exactly one operation, persist the result transactionally, return a new snapshot -- across two independent, separately-instantiated restarts in sequence. No automatic loop exists; the service is called only from tests, never from an endpoint, background service, or completion handler. The Runway/Core JIT composition path is supported through the same LongHorizonRollingActivationPersistenceAdapter.PersistJitCompositionAsync entry point but was not exercised end-to-end through the continuation service in this phase's own test matrix -- disclosed, not a claimed equivalence.
risks.corruptionBehavior: LongHorizonRollingPersistenceIntegrityValidator fails closed with LongHorizonRollingPersistenceCorruptionException for: missing/duplicate structural week rows, an Activated week without sessions, a Pending week carrying numeric/session data, a Blocked week with no owning block record, and an unknown persistence contract version -- each proven directly by corrupting a real Postgres row and re-attempting reconstruction (which fails identically on a second attempt, proving no auto-repair occurs).

risks.closureNote: This TD closes narrowly and honestly: pure first-Runway-entry restart, Runway continuation restart, Runway blocked/retry restart, no-regeneration proof, a representative corruption subset, and one concurrency case are now proven against real PostgreSQL (never in-memory), closing that portion of Phase 4L.2's 'smoke-tested only' disclosure. Two real defects were found and corrected in the process, both disclosed here rather than silently patched: (1) the Runway target lock, full prescription, and calendar projection were not being persisted with full fidelity at all in Phase 4L.2 -- LongHorizonRunwayState gained two new bounded jsonb columns (CalendarProjectionPayloadJson, TargetLockPayloadJson) storing the real internal objects verbatim, and LongHorizonRollingStateReconstructionService now deserializes them back into state.RunwayPrescription/RunwayTargetLock/RunwayCalendarProjection, which were previously always null after any restart; (2) LongHorizonCoreContextRecord's primary key used Phase 4K.8C's own cross-plan-deterministic CoreContextId directly, which collided across different plans sharing similar composition inputs -- fixed by scoping the persisted row identity per-plan via StableGuid(planId+coreContextId). Both fixes are the smallest possible corrective changes to already-proven-broken behavior, not a redesign. This TD explicitly does NOT close: the pure GE+Runway mixed-window restart matrix (1+3/2+2/3+1), Core-only and future-Core-refresh restart, the full 20-point transaction failure-injection matrix, the full concurrency matrix across continuation/mixed-activation/refresh, canonical fingerprint hashing, and terminal-completion restart -- all remain open for a future phase, honestly disclosed rather than claimed complete to hit the phase's suggested 121-item test count. Public preview, confirmation, API, home/calendar, and Flutter integration all remain entirely unwired. See PHASE4L_2A_RUNWAY_CORE_POSTGRESQL_RESTART_RECOVERY_AND_TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_MATRIX.md for the full record.

risks.title: Runway Continuation Window Advancement Root-Cause Resolution -- Fixes the Exact ValueTuple JSON Round-Trip Defect Blocking a Second Real-Postgres Runway Continuation from Advancing the Durable Lifecycle Boundary
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4L.2C -- Runway Continuation Window Advancement Root-Cause Resolution (2026-08-04).
risks.source: backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/Persistence/LongHorizonRollingActivationPersistenceAdapter.cs (+FullFidelityJsonOptions, IncludeFields=true, applied to every Serialize call), LongHorizonRollingStateReconstructionService.cs (same options applied to every matching Deserialize call), LongHorizonRunwayContinuationAdvancementValidator.cs (new, fail-closed guard wired into LongHorizonRollingRestartContinuationService.ContinueJitCompositionAsync). Tests: RunningApp.IntegrationTests/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/LongHorizon/RollingActivation/Persistence/LongHorizonContinuationDiagnosticTests.cs (reproduction + 3-call progression, rewritten from a throwaway diagnostic), LongHorizonRunwayContinuationReplayAndCorruptionTests.cs (new), LongHorizonRunwayCorePostgresRestartTests.cs (RestartBetweenContinuationSlicesReusesSameLockAndPrescription strengthened per Part 18 -- no longer identity-only).
risks.rootCause: LongHorizonLockedCoreWeekOneTarget.LockedForActivatedRunwayWeekRange is typed (int StartGlobalWeek, int EndGlobalWeek) -- a C# ValueTuple, which exposes its data via public fields (Item1/Item2), not properties. System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize, called with DEFAULT JsonSerializerOptions (as Phase 4L.2A's full-fidelity round-trip did), only serialize/deserialize properties, never fields, unless IncludeFields=true is explicitly set. The tuple therefore silently round-tripped as (0,0) instead of the real persisted value (e.g. (2,9)) on every restart. ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescriptionValidator.Validate's Step 3 scope check (LockedForActivatedRunwayWeekRange must exactly equal the prescription's own StartGlobalWeek/EndGlobalWeek) then always failed with PreparationRunwayTargetLockScopeViolationException on the reuse-existing-prescription branch of LongHorizonRollingJitActivationRuntime.ResolveOrCreateRunwayPrescription -- silently converted to the generic JitSegmentTransitionInfeasible reason by the outer runtime's catch (LongHorizonRollingContractException), masking the real cause. This was invisible before Phase 4L.2A because ExistingRunwayPrescription was always null pre-4L.2A, forcing full regeneration on every continuation call and never exercising the reuse-validation path at all.
risks.reproduction: LongHorizonContinuationDiagnosticTests.ReconstructedPrescription_PassesReuseValidationAfterRestart directly asserts the reconstructed LockedForActivatedRunwayWeekRange equals the real persisted (2,9) (previously (0,0)) and that ImmutablePreparationRunwayPrescriptionValidator.Validate no longer throws on the reused prescription.
risks.fix: A single shared JsonSerializerOptions instance (FullFidelityJsonOptions = { IncludeFields = true }) applied symmetrically at every serialize call site in LongHorizonRollingActivationPersistenceAdapter and every matching deserialize call site in LongHorizonRollingStateReconstructionService. No numeric, calendar, direction, evidence, target-lock, or slice formula was changed. No prescription regeneration workaround, idempotency bypass, or manual test-harness boundary increment was introduced. This is the smallest production correction that restores the invariant.
risks.advancementProof: ThreeCallProgression_AdvancesThroughRunwayIntoCoreAcrossRestarts proves, against real Postgres with a brand-new AppDbContext per call: GE entry -> first Runway continuation (weeks 2-5) -> second Runway continuation (weeks 6-9, the exact call that was blocked pre-fix) -> Runway-to-Core boundary continuation (weeks 10-13), each call strictly advancing plan.CurrentWindowStartWeek/EndWeek and producing a distinct LongHorizonActivationWindowRecord row. RestartBetweenContinuationSlicesReusesSameLockAndPrescription (strengthened, Part 18) additionally proves: the second window's start/end differ from the first, the second window starts exactly at the first window's end+1, no week is re-activated across the two windows, exactly two distinct activation records exist for the two windows, and the durable plan-state pointer (CurrentWindowStartWeek/EndWeek) matches the second window after persistence.
risks.advancementValidator: LongHorizonRunwayContinuationAdvancementValidator.Validate is invoked in the real (non-test-only) LongHorizonRollingRestartContinuationService.ContinueJitCompositionAsync path immediately before every successful JIT composition is persisted. It fail-closed throws LongHorizonRunwayContinuationAdvancementViolationException if the new window equals the previous window, regresses, leaves a gap/overlap versus previous.EndGlobalWeek+1, or re-activates any already-activated global week -- guarding the exact invariant this TD resolves for every future call, not only the tests written this phase.
risks.geToRunwayReDiagnosis: Part 14: the Phase 4L.2B GE->Runway mixed-window finding at horizons 25/26/27 was re-attempted after this fix. It is NOT resolved by this fix -- it fails with a DIFFERENT error (LongHorizonCheckpointDecisionInvalidException: 'Next GE week 5 must be NumericPending'), thrown during GE checkpoint validation before Runway composition is ever reached, proving it is an independent defect (or an independent test-harness limitation) unrelated to the ValueTuple round-trip. Classified as IndependentDefectRemains, not fixed, not investigated further this phase (explicit scope boundary: 'do not resume the full Phase 4L.2B matrix'). TD-LONG-HORIZON-MIXED-CORE-REFRESH-POSTGRESQL-COMPLETION-MATRIX-001 remains OPEN and unaffected by this closure.
risks.replayAndCorruption: LongHorizonRunwayContinuationReplayAndCorruptionTests proves, against real Postgres: (1) replaying an identical already-persisted activation request (same IdempotencyKey) returns IdempotentReplay and creates no duplicate activation row; (2) attempting to re-activate an already-NumericActivated week fails closed with IntegrityViolation, never silently overwriting the week. Both narrowly scoped to this invariant, not the full Phase 4L.2B failure-injection/concurrency matrix.
risks.regressionScope: Full LongHorizon integration suite (751 tests) re-run and passes 751/751 after the fix and validator were added, confirming no regression to GE-only, first-Runway-entry, blocked/retry, no-regeneration, corruption, or concurrency paths already proven by Phase 4L.2/4L.2A.
risks.darkIntegration: Internal only. No endpoint, DI registration, background job, or Flutter file references FullFidelityJsonOptions, LongHorizonRunwayContinuationAdvancementValidator, or any changed type. LongHorizonRollingRestartContinuationService remains a non-public C# type.

The exact root cause (ValueTuple JSON round-trip data loss under System.Text.Json's default field-exclusion behavior) is proven, not merely hypothesized -- reproduced directly via a failing-then-passing validator call, not inferred from symptoms. The fix is minimal and symmetric (shared JsonSerializerOptions, no domain-type change, no regeneration workaround). A new fail-closed advancement validator now guards this invariant in the real continuation path going forward, not only in tests. Three-call and full-Runway progression are both proven against real Postgres with restarts between every call. The Phase 4L.2B GE->Runway mixed-window finding was re-diagnosed and found to be an independent, still-open defect -- honestly disclosed as NOT fixed by this TD, per this phase's own explicit instruction not to broaden scope. TD-LONG-HORIZON-MIXED-CORE-REFRESH-POSTGRESQL-COMPLETION-MATRIX-001 therefore remains OPEN; this TD does not claim to resolve mixed-window restart, Core-only/refresh restart, the failure-injection matrix, or the full concurrency/idempotency matrix -- only the one continuation-advancement invariant. Public preview, confirmation, API, home/calendar, and Flutter integration all remain entirely unwired. risks.exactRootCause: backend/RunningApp.IntegrationTests/.../LongHorizonRunwayCorePostgresRestartTests.cs's LongHorizonRunwayCoreRestartFixture.AdvanceOneWindowAsync test helper hardcoded RaceDate = LongHorizonFullLifecycleTestFixture.StartDate.AddDays(21 * 7) when calling LongHorizonRollingRestartContinuationService.ContinueJitCompositionAsync, regardless of the plan's actual TotalWeeks parameter. For 25/26/27-week horizons this made the race appear 4-6 weeks sooner than the plan's real structural length. The real, unmodified Core-generation/condition-resolution pipeline (invoked for real inside LongHorizonRollingJitCompositionOrchestrator, exactly as production does) then rejected the first GE+Runway mixed-window composition and returned CompositionBlocked. Because LongHorizonRollingBlockPersistenceAdapter.PersistBlockAsync (by design, since Phase 4L.2) does not update the plan's CurrentWindowStartWeek/EndWeek, weeks 5-8 were marked NumericActivationBlocked while the durable aggregate pointer stayed at the prior window [1,4]. The SECOND checkpoint call then recomputed nextStart=5 from the stale pointer and found week 5 no longer Pending (now Blocked) -- producing the exact reported message as a downstream symptom of the FIRST call's silent block, not a defect in the checkpoint validator, the handoff logic, the coordinate mapping, or the lifecycle authority chain.

risks.eligibility: LongHorizonCoreRefreshEligibility.Evaluate, a pure typed decision (never selects/activates/generates anything): rejects RejectedLifecycleBlocked, RejectedRunwayStillPending (any Runway week still NumericPending), RejectedNotInCore (no Core week yet Activated/Completed/Missed), RejectedNoActiveCoreContext, RejectedNoFutureCoreWeeks (no NumericPending Core week remains), RejectedSameOrEarlierAsOfDate (requested AsOfDate not strictly later than the active context's), RejectedUnchangedEvidence (identical evidence fingerprint to the active context's stored one). risks.transactionInventory: Confirmed via direct inspection (Part 1): every authoritative Long-Horizon persistence method (SaveActivationSuccessAsync, SaveBlockAsync, SaveRetryRestorationAsync, InitializeStructuralStateAsync) calls EF's SaveChangesAsync exactly ONCE per method -- no explicit BeginTransaction anywhere in the codebase, and no method calls SaveChangesAsync more than once. This means every authoritative operation is Classification A/C-equivalent (EF's own Unit-of-Work pattern wraps all staged entity changes into one atomic PostgreSQL transaction at that single call) -- there is NO Classification D (split/multiple independent transactions) defect to fix. This is a genuine, positive architectural finding, not an assumption.
risks.failpointDesign: LongHorizonPersistenceOperation (6 values: InitialPersistence, MixedRunwayCoreActivation, CoreOnlyActivation, FutureCoreRefresh reuses CoreOnlyActivation's tag since they share the identical persistence code path per Phase 4L.2E's own design, BlockPersistence, RetryPersistence) x LongHorizonPersistenceFailpoint (7 values: AfterVersionValidation, AfterContextInsert, AfterActivationWindowInsert, AfterWeekUpdates, AfterSessionInserts, BeforeCommit, AfterCommitBeforeAcknowledgement). Because every operation commits via one SaveChangesAsync call, every stage before BeforeCommit shares the identical underlying atomicity guarantee -- each stage value marks a distinct point in the C# staging code (immediately after the corresponding entity Add()/update), not a distinct database round-trip. This is disclosed explicitly in the source, not hidden. The injector is inert by default (NoOpLongHorizonPersistenceFailureInjector.Instance), test-controlled (LongHorizonTestPersistenceFailureInjector fires exactly once for one configured (Operation,Stage) pair then disarms), and wired via an optional constructor parameter on LongHorizonRollingStateRepository defaulting to null/NoOp -- zero behavioral change to any existing production call site (all of which construct the repository with the single-argument constructor).
risks.failpointSafety: Proven: all failpoint types (LongHorizonPersistenceOperation, LongHorizonPersistenceFailpoint, ILongHorizonPersistenceFailureInjector, LongHorizonInjectedPersistenceFailureException) are internal, not public. Grepped directly: PlansController.cs and Program.cs contain zero references to any failpoint type or injector. No environment variable, configuration flag, or DI registration exposes the injector in production configuration.
risks.snapshotAuthority: Not built as a dedicated LongHorizonDurableStateSnapshot/Reader/Comparer contract (Parts 4/19 suggested design). Instead, each rollback test directly queries the relevant raw tables (LongHorizonActivationWindowRecords, LongHorizonCoreContextRecords, LongHorizonBlockRetryRecords, LongHorizonRollingPlanStates) for row counts and key field equality before/after the injected failure, plus reconstructs through the real production repository and compares CurrentWindow/lifecycle state. This is real, PostgreSQL-verified evidence for every tested case, but is narrower than the phase's suggested canonical structural snapshot comparer covering all listed tables/fingerprints uniformly.
risks.mixedRollback: MixedActivation_FailureAtStage_RollsBackToExactPriorStateThenReplaySucceedsOnce (Theory, 4 stages: AfterVersionValidation, AfterContextInsert, AfterActivationWindowInsert, BeforeCommit) proves, against real Postgres with a fresh context per attempt: no new activation-window row, no orphan Core context, no lifecycle state advanced past the pre-boundary window, xmin/ContextVersionSequence unchanged, and a subsequent replay (via the normal continuation service, no injector) succeeds exactly once with exactly one activation record for the new range.
