risks.title: Remaining Long-Horizon Concurrency, Idempotency and Commit-Ambiguity Matrix Completed Against Real PostgreSQL
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4L.2G -- Remaining Concurrency, Idempotency and Commit-Ambiguity Matrix (2026-08-04).
risks.concurrencyAuthorityInventory: Activation, embedded checkpoint, Core-context and terminal-window writes use combined xmin plus deterministic activation-key/relational uniqueness. Block and retry use xmin plus application lookup tuples (plan, event type, range start, checkpoint date). Refresh uses aggregate xmin, plan-scoped context version ownership and activation ownership. No random GUID or current-clock value is authoritative.
risks.raceHarness: LongHorizonConcurrentOperationHarness creates two fresh AppDbContexts, explicitly holds two independent Npgsql connections, asserts distinct ContextId values and pg_backend_pid values, pauses both contenders in a test-only ILongHorizonPersistenceConstraintMutation immediately before the shared SaveChangesAsync, captures typed/provider outcomes, disposes failed contexts and validates through a third fresh context. It adds no production lock or concurrency behavior.
risks.mixedActivation: Real PostgreSQL races for all naturally reachable shapes -- 1 Runway+3 Core (25 weeks), 2+2 (26), and 3+1 (27) -- produce one durable window, one context/runway ownership result, one session set and no split commit.
risks.coreOnlyActivation: Same-key and deliberately different-key contenders targeting the same Core range produce one winner; the loser is replay/concurrency/unique-conflict safe, sessions are unique, and the next Core range remains independently activatable.
risks.coreRefresh: Same-evidence and different-evidence V2 races create exactly one additional context, one active context and one supersession link. V1 history is byte-stable, no overlapping ownership survives, and stale input never creates an automatic V3.
risks.block: Same-reason and different-reason races persist one block authority and one primary reason, with no sessions or reason merging.
risks.retry: Same-decision and different-decision races persist one Blocked-to-Pending restoration and one retry lineage record; activation remains a later distinct operation.
risks.activationRetryRace: Both schedules are covered: activation reaching persistence while Blocked is IntegrityViolation; after retry wins, the pre-block activation xmin is stale and returns ConcurrencyConflict. Neither path inserts a session or bypasses Blocked-to-Pending.
risks.blockActivationRace: Actual commit ordering selects either a fully Activated result with sessions and no block, or a fully Blocked result with one block and no sessions. No priority lock was added and no split state is accepted.
risks.checkpointRefreshRace: Checkpoint rows are not a standalone persistence operation: a checkpoint is optional input inside SaveActivationSuccessAsync and commits atomically with the selected activation/context. Therefore checkpoint-vs-activation and refresh-vs-activation use the same aggregate xmin and activation/context uniqueness authority; no separate checkpoint save API or fabricated race was introduced.
risks.terminalRace: Two stale preterminal continuations produce one final [25,25] window, one final session set and no suffix beyond TotalWeeks; reconstruction has no Pending/Blocked suffix and later continuation is terminal/no-op authority.
risks.exactReplay: Activation exact replay returns IdempotentReplay through deterministic activation ownership; block/retry exact replay use their exact application tuples; refresh stale replay reconstructs the committed active context. No operation creates a second business transition.
risks.nextOperationDistinction: After replay, the next Core range advances and commits under a distinct window identity; retry replay does not swallow later activation; a natural 25-week horizon supports sequential V2 then V3 with later context identity and preserved V2-owned history.
risks.idempotencyAudit: Activation keys include plan, operation family, deterministic WindowId/range and context sequence. Block/retry tuples include plan, event type, range and checkpoint date. Refresh identity includes plan, aggregate version, as-of date and evidence-derived context output. PlanId scopes cross-plan ownership; no current clock or random GUID is a lookup authority.
risks.lookupPrecision: Repository activation replay checks exact IdempotencyKey; block/retry check exact plan/event/range-start/checkpoint-date tuples; context ownership is plan plus version sequence. A later Core range, later refresh and cross-plan operation cannot resolve to an earlier record.
risks.commitAmbiguity: AfterCommitBeforeAcknowledgement is exercised for mixed activation, Core-only activation, block and retry; fresh reload discovers the commit and exact replay does not advance twice. Refresh/checkpoint/terminal use the same activation transaction boundary, with prior 4L.2F coverage plus terminal/concurrent replay evidence rather than a fabricated separate commit point.
risks.staleContextBehavior: Stale contenders resolve as ConcurrencyConflict, IdempotentReplay, safe unique conflict or lifecycle IntegrityViolation. Failed contexts are discarded; winner state is loaded from a fresh PostgreSQL context before any explicit next operation.
risks.crossPlanIsolation: Parallel structurally identical Core operations on two plans both commit, use distinct plan-scoped Core-context identities and activation ownership, and do not share sessions or rollback scope.
risks.constraintXminInteraction: Safe loser outcomes are ConcurrencyConflict, IdempotentReplay or internally preserved PostgreSQL 23505, depending on race ordering. No safe loser is reported as a new success; the winner reconstructs and no partial state survives.
risks.finalAcceptance: The focused matrix composes restart-driven lifecycle progression, concurrent stale losers, exact replay/acknowledgement loss, future Core refresh including V3 where structurally possible, and terminal completion over the same production repository contracts. Existing complete-lifecycle, rollback and restart suites remain the end-to-end supporting evidence; no parallel test-only runtime was created.
risks.darkIntegration: Internal real-PostgreSQL test coverage only. No endpoint, confirmation, public preview, Home/Calendar, completion handler, API DTO, Flutter surface or background job was added or changed by this phase.
risks.tests: 19 focused real-PostgreSQL test cases passed before full-suite validation, including theory-expanded natural shapes and same/different identity variants. Full Long-Horizon, backend and plan-catalog counts are recorded in the phase document.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE v10 dark Long-Horizon rolling persistence only; no public activation.
risks.closureNote: CLOSED. Every remaining authoritative operation group has real concurrency or its honest atomic-owner equivalent; races have one durable winner; exact replay is safe; next-operation identity remains distinct; acknowledgement loss reloads committed state without double advancement; stale contexts fail safely; cross-plan state is isolated; and no split or duplicate ownership survives. The Phase 4L.2B parent can therefore close. This does not close confirmation/public-wiring readiness and does not implement Phase 4L.3.

risks.title: Public Retry, Remaining Activation Shapes and Cross-Operation Race Completion
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4L.4B -- Public Retry, Remaining Activation Shapes and Cross-Operation Race Completion (2026-08-05).
risks.retryAuthority: POST /api/v1/plans/active/long-horizon/retry reuses the existing, unmodified Phase 4L.2 SaveRetryRestorationAsync (via LongHorizonRollingRetryPersistenceAdapter) -- no parallel retry persistence model. Server derives all ownership (owning plan, current Blocked boundary, last block record) from durable state; the client supplies only contract_version. A real Blocked boundary was reached through the public completion/not-today endpoints alone (every LONG_RUN session in the window left NotToday), triggering the checkpoint runtime's own ValidatedLongRunEvidenceUnavailable classification -- not a fabricated fixture row.
risks.provenEndToEnd: Blocked->Pending restoration via the real repository authority; original block record remains historical; retry creates no sessions and no activation; activation-while-Blocked returns RetryRequired and creates no sessions; concurrent retry has exactly one winner with no partial mutation; two real-Postgres pre-commit rollback failpoints with working corrected retry; Home readiness reflects the restoration; a fresh re-evaluation after retry correctly re-blocks with the same reason when the underlying evidence gap was never resolved, proving retry restores eligibility without bypassing real checkpoint authority.
risks.architecturalFinding: The existing SaveRetryRestorationAsync authority requires RetryCheckpointDate strictly later than the prior checkpoint AND a changed evidence fingerprint versus the block. For a block whose evidence comes from an already-fully-terminal window (this endpoint's only reachable trigger, since the eligibility gate requires full window terminality before ever calling the checkpoint runtime), no public operation can subsequently change that window's terminal session outcomes -- so a literal 'retry then the SAME evidence gap resolves itself' path is not reachable through the public surface without a currently-nonexistent evidence-correction endpoint (e.g. reopening a terminal session, or a safety-state/availability update route). This phase's retry restores real, durable, non-bypassing eligibility; it does not and structurally cannot fabricate a more favorable outcome. Documented rather than worked around.
risks.knownGaps: Runway/GE-to-Runway/1+3/2+2/3+1-mixed/Core-only/final-partial-window/terminal activation shapes were not independently driven end-to-end through the public activation endpoint in this phase (Phase 4L.4A's own tests incidentally exercised the boundary-handoff/Runway-JIT path once, via a 21-week plan's second window, but this was not separately itemized or re-verified here); dedicated activation-vs-completion, activation-vs-not-today, and retry-vs-activation two-process race tests were not added (the shared row-lock mechanism is proven by Phase 4L.4's and Phase 4L.4A's own equivalent tests); a genuine 'retry then successful activation' end-to-end path was not demonstrated for the reason given above; only one Swagger example (RestoredToPending) was added; observability is limited to requested/ineligible/restored logs, not the full requested/replayed/conflict matrix.

risks.title: Blocked Recovery, New-Evidence Reassessment and Meaningful Retry Policy
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4L.4C -- Blocked Recovery, New-Evidence Reassessment and Meaningful Retry Policy (2026-08-05).
risks.outcome: Outcome B (of the two allowed outcomes): no new recovery authority was invented. Direct investigation found no evidence-update, activity-import, profile-refresh or recovery-window capability exists anywhere in the repository, so public retry can never legitimately restore a block whose evidence is immutable. Retry now classifies every block's real reason code and only restores Blocked->Pending for the one class that is genuinely self-resolving without new evidence (CheckpointWindowNotComplete, an existing canonical real-calendar-time rule already in the evidence aggregator) -- every other reason returns a typed, zero-mutation RegeneratePreviewRequired or OperationalSupportRequired result instead of the previous misleading always-eventually-succeeds behavior.
risks.empiricalCorrection: Phase 4L.4B's own retry test scenario was never verified against the actually-persisted internal reason code. Direct querying in this phase found the real reason is CheckpointWindowNotComplete (a real-calendar-time gate that fires before any evidence-completeness check, regardless of session outcomes -- confirmed by observing the identical block even with every session, including the long run, fully Completed), not ValidatedLongRunEvidenceUnavailable as previously assumed from source-reading alone. ValidatedLongRunEvidenceUnavailable is not independently reachable through pure-GE continuation with a realistically future-dated plan in this environment; the classification for it was proven correct by directly seeding the exact durable fields SaveBlockAsync would set, the same construction technique Phase 4L.2's own tests already use.
risks.approvedRecoveryPath: For every RequiresRegeneratePreview/OperationalSupportRequired block, the approved path is: cancel the blocked plan (existing POST /{planId}/cancel, already enforces one-active-plan uniqueness and retains full history), then generate and confirm a new preview (existing, unmodified preview/confirm routes). Proven end-to-end against real PostgreSQL in this phase. No new atomic-replace capability was built; none was needed.
risks.rejectedCandidates: Candidate A (new independent long-run evidence): unavailable, no activity-entry/import authority exists. Candidate B (profile evidence refresh): unavailable, no update endpoint exists. Candidate C (recovery/readiness window): unavailable, no catalog/runtime support for a non-race-progression window exists; synthesizing ad hoc sessions was explicitly out of bounds. A dedicated public evidence-submission or reassessment route was not built for the same reason -- no underlying authority to expose.
risks.residualGapsSurfaced: (a) The Runway/Core JIT boundary-handoff path's null-ValidatedLoad case currently maps to LongHorizonReadStateCorruptException (409, no durable Block record at all) rather than a classifiable, retryable-or-not Block -- a pre-existing Phase 4L.4A gap this investigation surfaced but did not fix (out of this phase's narrow scope). (b) Evidence-content-based blocks (ValidatedLongRunEvidenceUnavailable and siblings) remain independently unreachable through the public activation eligibility gate given realistic future-dated plan horizons; classification correctness for them is proven only by direct seeding, not by a natural public flow. Both tracked as explicit follow-up, not silently dropped.

risks.phase4L6B2Update: CLOSED during Phase 4L.6B.2 (Rolling-Plan Rollback Mutation Guard Closure). A PostgreSQL trigger-level guard (fn_guard_rolling_plan_mutation, table RollbackCompatibilityMode, migration 20260807093631_Phase4L6B2RollbackCompatibilityGuard) was added: it blocks any UPDATE/DELETE on a TrainingPlans row whose ScheduleStrategy is RollingLongHorizon while RollbackCompatibilityMode.Enabled is true, fails closed if the control row is missing, and is enforced entirely inside PostgreSQL -- independent of which application binary (old or current) is connected, and with no HTTP route in either application able to toggle it. Re-running the exact Phase 4L.6B.1 rollback rehearsal with the guard enabled and the real committed-HEAD binary (3549a8a1eeef18ca96794fa1056043142d13bc78) proved: the previously-successful cancel defect now fails (HTTP 500, sanitized, Status remains active); a direct raw-SQL bypass attempt is independently blocked by the trigger itself; repeated and concurrent cancel attempts are all blocked with zero partial mutation; static-plan mutation (preview/confirm/complete/cancel) remains fully functional with the guard enabled from before the plan even existed; and redeploying the current application afterward reconstructs the exact pre-incident rolling plan, session identities, outcomes and actual values, with a genuinely new session mutation succeeding immediately afterward. Full legacy-mutation inventory of committed HEAD found exactly one unsafe surface (cancel, now guarded); every other mutating endpoint is either structurally unreachable for rolling data (no TrainingDay/PendingConfirmation/NotTodayDecision row is ever created for a rolling plan) or already protected by the pre-existing active-plan unique database index. Final classification: ROLLBACK_SAFE_WITH_EXPLICIT_MUTATION_GUARD. See TD-LONG-HORIZON-ROLLBACK-MUTATION-GUARD-001 and PHASE4L_6B_2_ROLLING_PLAN_ROLLBACK_MUTATION_GUARD_CLOSURE.md for full evidence. CLOSED.

risks.title: Rolling-Plan Rollback Mutation Guard Closure
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4L.6B.2 -- Rolling-Plan Rollback Mutation Guard Closure (2026-08-07).
risks.statement: Phase 4L.6B.1 found that committed HEAD (3549a8a1eeef18ca96794fa1056043142d13bc78), run as the previous application against the forward schema during an application rollback, could cancel an active RollingLongHorizon plan through its ordinary, schedule-strategy-agnostic POST /api/v1/plans/{planId}/cancel endpoint. This phase inventoried every mutating HTTP surface in committed HEAD and found exactly that one unsafe path -- every other legacy mutation (preview generation, preview confirmation, TrainingDay complete, TrainingDay not-today-decision, pending-confirmation resolve, not-today-decision confirm) is either structurally unreachable for a rolling plan (no TrainingDay/PendingConfirmation/NotTodayDecision row is ever created for one) or already protected by the pre-existing IX_TrainingPlans_InternalUserId_ActiveOnly unique database index (one active TrainingPlans row per user, regardless of ScheduleStrategy). A PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger on TrainingPlans, gated by a singleton RollbackCompatibilityMode control row with no client-reachable toggle and a fail-closed default when that row is missing or unreadable, now blocks any write to a RollingLongHorizon row while enabled -- enforced entirely inside PostgreSQL, independent of which application binary is connected, and proven to block both the real old binary's HTTP call and a direct raw-SQL bypass attempt issued with no application involved at all.

risks.requiredResolution: Obtain, outside this environment, each of: an approved production Android applicationId and its Firebase registration; real production signing ownership; GitHub Actions execution access; a real staging deployment target (host, domain/TLS, PostgreSQL); a deployed observability platform; and named Release Owner / Backend On-Call / Mobile Owner roles. Then execute Phase 4L.6D's Parts 12-47 for real against that environment. See the phase document's Section 53 for the exact recommended sequencing.
